labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
The current `/goal` system (hermes_cli/goals.py) is documented as if it cleanly
hands work off to the Kanban dispatcher for multi-agent execution, but source
verification shows it does not. This issue flags the contradiction so the docs
or behaviour can be aligned.

## What I verified

Full code audit at hermes-agent commit c23a87bc163b188abc7e40fbdccf07a9739231c3. Findings:

1. **`goals.py` imports (lines 31–38) contain zero kanban modules.**
   `kanban`, `kanban_db`, `kanban_tools`, and `dispatch_once` do not appear
   anywhere in `goals.py` (full-file grep returns no matches).

2. **`GoalManager.evaluate_after_turn` (`goals.py:461–576`) is a same-session
   loop.** When `should_continue: True`, it fires `next_continuation_prompt()`
   (`goals.py:578–581`) as a normal user-role message into the existing
   `run_conversation`. No subprocess spawn, no Kanban write, no
   cross-profile dispatch.

3. **Kanban tools are gated behind `_check_kanban_mode()`
   (`kanban_tools.py:59–73`).** The tools are only visible to the model when
   either `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` env var is set (dispatcher-spawned worker)
   OR the profile's `config.yaml` has `kanban` in its `toolsets` list.
   A standard chat session does not see `kanban_create`.

4. **`dispatch_once` (`kanban_db.py:3666`) is triggered only by the
   gateway-embedded dispatcher loop or `hermes kanban watch`.** Not by
   `/goal` evaluation.

## Why this matters

The docs around `/goal` (module docstring `goals.py:1–28`) describe a
continuation loop accurately, but downstream user-facing guidance (and at
least one community reference) treats `/goal` as the entry point for
multi-step decompositions that ultimately land on Kanban for parallel
worker execution. Users are setting goals expecting them to fan out across
agents; they instead burn turn budget in a single session.

## Suggested resolution paths (pick one)

- **Option A — docs only**: clarify in `/goal` help text and the module
  docstring that this is a same-session loop and explicitly point users at
  `kanban_create` (or a Kanban-toolset profile) for cross-agent dispatch.
- **Option B — code**: add an optional `--decompose` flag (or `kanban: true`
  in goal metadata) that runs the goal's first turn through a
  decomposition prompt and writes `kanban_create` cards rather than
  re-entering the same session.

Either is fine for our use case; we have a local workaround (Path A in our
internal architecture notes: an explicit `hermes-build-orchestrator`
profile with `kanban` in its `toolsets` that calls `kanban_create`
directly). Filing this so the gap is visible upstream.

## Versions

- hermes-agent: <fill in current sha from `git rev-parse HEAD` in
  ~/.hermes/hermes-agent>
- Python: 3.11+

items.title: [Bug] Credential pool rotation never fires when user interrupts retry loop between 429s (has_retried_429 flag lost on cancel)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

When a user interrupts (Ctrl-C / cancel) the retry loop **between** the first 429 and the rotation attempt, the `has_retried_429` flag (local var in `_recover_with_credential_pool`) is lost. The next user prompt restarts the retry sequence with `has_retried_429 = False`, so the agent goes through "first 429 → no rotate, retry same cred" forever — never reaching the second 429 that would trigger `pool.mark_exhausted_and_rotate()`.

In CEO-grade interactive workloads (lots of cancels + restarts), this means a credential pool with multiple healthy entries can stay stuck on a single exhausted credential indefinitely, even with retries, fallbacks and reset timers all configured.

Related but not duplicate:
- #22212 (rotation incomplete within a single retry burst) — same operator-visible symptom under different trigger
- #16830 (retry counter shared across pool entries) — different mechanism, also blocks deep pool usage

## Environment

- `hermes-agent` v0.11.0, gateway mode (`hermes gateway run`)
- Provider: `openai-codex` (ChatGPT Plus OAuth)
- Pool: 3 OAuth credentials, `fill_first` strategy
  - cred A: priority 0, plan_type `plus`, status `exhausted (429)` with `resets_at` in the future
  - cred B: priority 1, plan_type `plus`, status `exhausted (429)` with same `resets_at`
  - cred C: priority 2, plan_type `prolite`, status `null` (fresh, never used)
- Interactive frontend with mid-stream cancel support (e.g. Telegram bridge, TUI gateway).

## Observable behavior — bucle infinito sin rotación

```
⚠️  API call failed (attempt 1/3): RateLimitError [HTTP 429]
   🔌 Provider: openai-codex  Model: gpt-5.5
   📝 Error: HTTP 429: The usage limit has been reached
   📋 Details: {'plan_type': 'plus', 'resets_at': 1778767741, ...}
⏱️ Rate limited. Waiting 2.9s (attempt 2/3)...
⚡ Interrupted during API call.                  ← user cancels here

[next user prompt]
⚠️  API call failed (attempt 1/3): RateLimitError [HTTP 429]
   🔌 Provider: openai-codex  Model: gpt-5.5
   📝 Error: HTTP 429
⏱️ Rate limited. Waiting 2.9s (attempt 2/3)...
⚡ Interrupted during API call.                  ← repeat...
```

Grepping for rotation evidence:

```
$ docker logs hermes | grep -iE 'rotat|credential.*pool|exhausted'
(0 lines)
```

No rotation ever happens despite `oauth-3` being a fresh, never-used credential at priority 2.

`hermes auth list` showed `current_id` pointing to `oauth-1` continuously even after hours of 429s. `auth.json` `last_status` never got updated to `exhausted` for `oauth-1` because the rotation that writes that field never executed.

## Root cause hypothesis

The flag `has_retried_429` in `run_agent.py:_recover_with_credential_pool` is a **local variable in the retry loop**, not persisted to the agent state. When the user interrupts mid-retry:

1. Loop is aborted (raises `KeyboardInterrupt` or equivalent).
2. Local state inside the retry loop (including `has_retried_429`) is garbage collected.
3. Next user prompt creates a fresh retry context with `has_retried_429 = False`.
4. First 429 hits → `if not has_retried_429: return False, True` → retry same credential.
5. Before second 429 arrives, user often cancels again (high-cancel interactive workload).
6. Goto 3.

The rotation branch (`pool.mark_exhausted_and_rotate()`) requires reaching the SECOND 429 in the SAME retry burst, which is unreachable when each burst gets cancelled at attempt 1/3 or 2/3.

Code paths examined (paths relative to the installed package):
- `agent/credential_pool.py:_select_unlocked()` (l.728) — correct, picks fill_first
- `agent/credential_pool.py:_available_entries()` (l.671) — correct, skips exhausted with future reset
- `agent/credential_pool.py:mark_exhausted_and_rotate()` (l.765) — correct, but never reached in this scenario
- `run_agent.py:_recover_with_credential_pool()` (l.5146) — flag scope is the bug
- `run_agent.py:10175` — retry loop hook call site

## Reproduction

1. Configure `auth.json` with at least 2 credentials in the `openai-codex` pool; force one into `exhausted` state OR rate-limit it via real traffic.
2. Start `hermes gateway` and connect with any frontend that supports mid-stream cancel (TUI gateway, bridge-style chat frontend, etc.).
3. Send a prompt → observe first 429 → **immediately cancel** (Ctrl-C / frontend cancel button).
4. Send another prompt → observe first 429 again → cancel again.
5. Repeat 5-10 times.
6. Verify `hermes` server logs `grep -i rotat` returns 0 hits.
7. Verify `auth.json` `last_status` for the rate-limited credential was NEVER updated to `exhausted`.

Without the cancels (uninterrupted load), the rotation eventually fires and the bug doesn't reproduce. The cancellation pattern is the trigger.

## Proposed fixes

### Option A — minimal, defensive

Inside `_recover_with_credential_pool`, when `FailoverReason.rate_limit` AND `current.last_status == "exhausted"`, rotate **immediately** without waiting for the second 429. There is no point retrying a credential that is already marked exhausted in the pool state.

```python
if effective_reason == FailoverReason.rate_limit:
    current_entry = pool.get_current_entry()
    if current_entry and current_entry.last_status == "exhausted":
        # Already known exhausted, rotate immediately
        next_entry = pool.mark_exhausted_and_rotate(...)
        if next_entry is not None:
            self._swap_credential(next_entry)
            return True, False
    if not has_retried_429:
        return False, True
    # ... existing logic ...
```

### Option B — structural

Persist `has_retried_429` per `(session_id, credential_id)` on the agent state (e.g. `self._retried_429_for_credentials: set[str]`), survives interrupts and prompt boundaries. First 429 on a credential always retries; second 429 on the SAME credential anywhere in the session triggers rotation regardless of intermediate cancels.

This also handles the cross-prompt case correctly: a user who interrupts at attempt 2/3 and immediately re-sends should hit the rotation branch on the very next 429.

### Option C — both, with priority A → B

A is a 5-line guard that ships today. B is the proper fix that takes longer.

## Workaround (currently applied)

Manually reorder pool priorities in `auth.json` so the fresh credential is at priority 0 and the exhausted ones at priorities 1 and 2. Then restart the gateway so the in-memory pool reloads from disk.

```bash
# Pseudocode — adjust to your `auth.json` location and credential IDs
edit auth.json:
  set credential_pool.openai-codex[fresh-cred-id].priority = 0
  set credential_pool.openai-codex[exhausted-cred-1-id].priority = 1
  set credential_pool.openai-codex[exhausted-cred-2-id].priority = 2
restart hermes gateway
```

`_select_unlocked()` then picks the fresh credential on agent construction. No rotation needed while it has quota. When the exhausted credentials' `resets_at` timestamps lapse, they re-enter the pool naturally at priorities 1 and 2 — zero capacity loss.

This avoids the bug entirely by removing the need to rotate, at the cost of manually maintaining priorities.

## Suggested test coverage

```python
def test_credential_pool_rotates_after_interrupt_resume():
    """Interrupting the retry loop should not lose the rotation state."""
    pool = make_pool([
        Credential(id="A", status="active"),  # will get 429
        Credential(id="B", status="active"),  # healthy
    ])
    agent = make_agent(pool=pool)

    # First user request: simulate first 429, then immediate cancel
    with pytest.raises(KeyboardInterrupt):
        agent.respond("prompt 1", inject_429_on_call=1, cancel_after_attempt=2)

    # Second user request: should detect A is exhausted, rotate to B
    response = agent.respond("prompt 2", inject_429_on_call=1)
    assert pool.get_current_entry().id == "B"
    assert response  # no infinite loop
```

## Observability suggestion

Add a structured log line every time `_recover_with_credential_pool` decides NOT to rotate but TO retry, so operators can spot the "stuck retrying same exhausted credential" pattern in production:

```json
{"event":"credential_pool_retry_decision",
 "provider":"openai-codex",
 "current_id":"<sha>",
 "current_status":"<status>",
 "has_retried_429":false,
 "decision":"retry_same",
 "reason":"first_429_no_rotation_yet"}
```

Today there is zero log output from this branch, making the bug invisible from logs alone (we had to read the code to find it).

---

Filed by an operator running a multi-credential Codex pool in production behind an interactive frontend. Happy to provide further logs or test on a patched build.

**Example:** `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` appears in `hermes setup model` but does NOT appear in the `/model` picker.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `minimax-cn` provider with API key (`MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY`)
2. Run `hermes setup model` → the wizard fetches live models from `models.dev` API
3. Observe that `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` is listed as an available model
4. Start a chat session: `hermes chat`
5. Type `/model` to open the model picker
6. Observe that `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` is NOT listed (only `MiniMax-M2.7`, `MiniMax-M2.5`, `MiniMax-M2.1`, `MiniMax-M2` appear)

## Expected Behavior

The `/model` slash command picker should display the same model list as `hermes setup model` for a given provider.

## Actual Behavior

The `/model` picker uses `provider_model_ids()` → `_PROVIDER_MODELS` (static dict), while `hermes setup model` uses `fetch_models_dev()` (live API). Providers NOT in `_MODELS_DEV_PREFERRED` never merge with the live `models.dev` catalog in the `/model` picker path.

## Root Cause Analysis

In `hermes_cli/models.py`:

1. **`hermes setup model`** → `fetch_models_dev()` → live `models.dev` REST API (full catalog including variant models like `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`)

2. **`/model` picker** → `list_authenticated_providers()` → `provider_model_ids()`:
   ```python
   # line 2290-2293
   curated_static = list(_PROVIDER_MODELS.get(normalized, []))
   if normalized in _MODELS_DEV_PREFERRED:
       return _merge_with_models_dev(normalized, curated_static)
   return curated_static  # ← minimax-cn is NOT in _MODELS_DEV_PREFERRED
   ```

3. **`_PROVIDER_MODELS["minimax-cn"]`** (line 286-291) only lists:
   ```python
   "minimax-cn": [
       "MiniMax-M2.7",
       "MiniMax-M2.5",
       "MiniMax-M2.1",
       "MiniMax-M2",
   ],
   ```
   The `highspeed` variant is missing because it only exists in the `minimax-oauth` static list.

4. **`minimax-cn` is not in `_MODELS_DEV_PREFERRED`** (line 2085-2101), so the live `models.dev` merge never happens for this provider in the `/model` picker path.

## Proposed Fix

**Option A (preferred):** Add `"minimax-cn"` to `_MODELS_DEV_PREFERRED` in `hermes_cli/models.py`. This automatically brings all future `models.dev` entries for `minimax-cn` without requiring a Hermes release for each new model variant.

**Option B:** Add `"MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed"` directly to `_PROVIDER_MODELS["minimax-cn"]`. Simple but requires a release for each new variant.

## Related Issues

- **#23359** (tracking): provider/model inventory has no scriptable surface — four issues blocked, including this discrepancy between UI surfaces
- **#25542**: Add China-region (minimax-cn) OAuth provider — related minimax-cn provider exposure gap
- **#26130**: fix: add deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash to Nous Portal curated model list — same class of static-list-vs-live-catalog mismatch
- **#26016**: fix(model): require confirmation for very expensive model selections — `/model` picker UI improvements

## Environment

- OS: WSL (Linux)
- Hermes Version: 2.x (main branch)
- Provider: minimax-cn (MiniMax China direct API)

items.title: ux(telegram): sendMessageDraft (native draft streaming) causes visible content flicker/rollback in DM responses
items.body:
## Description

When using Hermes Agent via Telegram DM, responses exhibit a noticeable flicker/rollback effect: the first portion of the reply appears, then partially disappears, then more content appears — cycling until the final `sendMessage` completes.

This was introduced by commit `4ed293b38` (`feat(telegram): native draft streaming via sendMessageDraft (Bot API 9.5+)`), which defaults `transport` to `auto`. On DMs with PTB ≥ 22.6, `supports_draft_streaming` returns `True` and the consumer routes mid-stream frames through `sendMessageDraft` instead of progressive `editMessageText`.

## Root Cause

`sendMessageDraft` frames are "typing preview" animations in the Telegram client — not real messages. Each time a new draft frame is sent with the same `draft_id` but more accumulated text, the Telegram client **re-renders the preview from scratch**: existing content briefly collapses or disappears before the updated text renders. This is Telegram client behavior, not a Hermes bug per se, but the UX result is worse than the legacy edit-based path for most users.

The effect is especially noticeable on longer responses (tool-call chains, multi-paragraph answers).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes gateway with default config (PTB ≥ 22.6, no `streaming.transport` override)
2. Send a query to the Telegram DM that produces a moderately long response (300+ chars)
3. Observe the response: content appears, partially collapses, then grows again — repeating until the final `sendMessage` lands

## Expected Behavior

Content streams in progressively without any visible rollback, as with the legacy `editMessageText` path.

## Actual Behavior

Each draft frame update causes the Telegram client to briefly collapse/re-render the preview, giving the impression of content disappearing and reappearing.

## Environment

- Hermes gateway running on Linux (Ubuntu 24.04)
- python-telegram-bot 22.6
- Telegram clients tested: iOS, Desktop
- `streaming.transport` not set (defaults to `auto`)

## Workaround

Add to `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:

```yaml
streaming:
  transport: edit
```

This forces the legacy `editMessageText` path and eliminates the flicker entirely.

## Suggestions

1. **Change the default back to `transport: edit`** until the draft-streaming UX is validated across Telegram clients, or
2. **Add a per-platform opt-in** (e.g. `streaming.platforms.telegram.transport: draft`) so users can enable it deliberately, or
3. **Document the workaround** prominently in the streaming config reference so affected users can self-serve

The `transport: edit` → `transport: auto` default flip affects all DM users on PTB ≥ 22.6 without any opt-in, which seems premature given the client-side rendering behavior.

items.title: Agent lacks guidance to check own docs/source when uncertain about its capabilities

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

When Hermes Agent is uncertain about its own capabilities — whether a feature exists, how something is configured, what a tool does — it currently has no trigger to check its documentation or source code before answering. The only existing guidance is `HERMES_AGENT_HELP_GUIDANCE` in `agent/prompt_builder.py`, which fires on this narrow trigger:

> "If the user asks about configuring, setting up, or using Hermes Agent itself..."

This misses:
- "Does Hermes support X?" (capability question, not setup question)
- "How does feature Y work?" (knowledge question)
- General uncertainty about own capabilities

## Symptom

The agent confidently claims a feature does not exist rather than checking. This has been corrected in practice (SOUL.md now warns against it) but the system prompt guidance was never updated to match. The fix needs to be in the mechanism, not just the meta-instruction.

## Proposed Fix

Two changes:

1. **Widen `HERMES_AGENT_HELP_GUIDANCE`** in `agent/prompt_builder.py` — add uncertainty triggers: "if you are uncertain about your own capabilities, if cached knowledge about a feature seems stale or incomplete"

2. **Add `references/live-documentation-sources.md`** to the bundled `hermes-agent` skill — a structured reference table mapping Hermes feature categories (config, CLI, tools, MCP, gateway, etc.) to docs URLs, source code paths, and verification commands. This gives the agent a concrete lookup path when the trigger fires.

## Design Principle

Hermes is open source and locally installed. This is a unique advantage over proprietary coding agents — the agent can read the actual source code as ground truth when docs are ambiguous. The three-tier fallback (docs → source code → verification command) is only possible because of Hermes openness.

This must be an original approach, not a copy of any proprietary system implementation. The architecture (trigger in guidance + on-demand skill reference) is a natural fit for Hermes' skill-based design, at zero token cost when not triggered.

items.title: `hermes update` on forks reports "Already up to date!" when origin/main matches HEAD but upstream/main is ahead

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Description

On a fork of hermes-agent, `hermes update` can silently no-op even when `upstream/main` has new commits, because the early-return branch in `_cmd_update_impl()` checks against `origin/main` only and never consults `upstream/main` before bailing.

This is the apply-path counterpart to the bug #19696 fixed for the `--check` path.

## Repro

1. Fork the repo, clone your fork.
2. Let your fork's `origin/main` fall behind `upstream/main` (i.e. don't sync the fork's default branch).
3. Locally, `git pull origin main` so local HEAD == `origin/main`.
4. Run `hermes update`.

**Expected:** updates pulled from `upstream/main`.
**Actual:** "✓ Already up to date!" — upstream is never consulted.

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/main.py` `_cmd_update_impl()`:

- Line ~7698: `git rev-list HEAD..origin/{branch} --count` — counts only against `origin`, so forks lagging upstream see `commit_count == 0`.
- Line ~7707: in the `commit_count == 0` early-return, `_sync_with_upstream_if_needed()` is never called, so the fork never pulls from upstream.

## Relationship to #19696

#19696 (merged) fixed the analogous bug in `_cmd_update_check()` (the `hermes update --check` probe) by fetching `upstream` first and falling back to `origin`. The apply path (`_cmd_update_impl()`) was not touched.

## Proposed fix

PR #4873 adds the missing `_sync_with_upstream_if_needed()` call to the early-return path, gated on `is_fork and branch == "main"`.

A broader follow-up (or expanded scope on #4873) should also fix the `HEAD..origin/{branch}` count itself so forks aren't blind to upstream on the non-early-return path either.

## Platforms

- macOS (Apple Silicon) — reproduced

items.title: [Bug]: Kanban max_runtime_seconds does not align terminal command timeout
items.body:
## Bug Description

Kanban tasks can set `max_runtime_seconds` to allow a worker attempt to run for a long time, but the worker's `terminal` tool still inherits the generic `terminal.timeout` / `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT` default.

That creates two independent timeout budgets:

- Kanban worker runtime: controlled by task `max_runtime_seconds`
- Terminal command runtime: controlled by `terminal.timeout`

For long-running Kanban work, a task can allow a worker to run for 3600 seconds while a foreground terminal command still times out after the global terminal default. The worker may then continue from a partial command result, retry repeatedly, or complete/block based on a timeout that did not reflect the task's runtime budget.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a normal terminal timeout, for example `terminal.timeout: 180`.
2. Create a Kanban task with a longer runtime cap, for example `max_runtime_seconds: 3600`.
3. Let the dispatcher spawn the worker.
4. Inside the worker, run a foreground terminal command that legitimately needs more than 180 seconds but less than the Kanban task runtime.

## Expected Behavior

A dispatched Kanban worker with a task-level `max_runtime_seconds` should get a terminal default timeout that is consistent with that task runtime, without requiring the model to remember to pass an explicit `timeout` argument on every terminal call.

The terminal timeout should still leave a small grace window so the worker can observe a command timeout and call `kanban_block` or `kanban_complete` before the dispatcher kills the whole worker attempt.

## Actual Behavior

The worker inherits the generic `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT` from the parent process. That value may be much shorter than `max_runtime_seconds`, so the terminal command can be killed well before the Kanban worker runtime expires.

## Affected Component

- Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)
- Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)
- Other: Kanban dispatcher / worker runtime

## Messaging Platform

N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

Not available. This was reproduced and fixed from source-level inspection plus targeted local regression tests.

## Operating System

Linux / WSL-style development environment

## Python Version

Python 3.13 test environment

## Hermes Version

Current `main` branch

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

Before the fix, Kanban worker spawn only copied the parent process environment and did not adjust `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT` for `max_runtime_seconds`.

After the fix, a task with `max_runtime_seconds=3600` and inherited `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT=180` spawns the worker with:

```text
TERMINAL_TIMEOUT=3570
TERMINAL_MAX_FOREGROUND_TIMEOUT=3570
```

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::_default_spawn()` builds worker subprocess environment with `env = dict(os.environ)`. The terminal tool reads its default timeout from `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT`, which is bridged from `terminal.timeout` by the CLI and gateway config loaders.

`max_runtime_seconds` is stored on the Kanban task and enforced by the dispatcher, but it was not reflected in the worker's terminal environment. As a result, Kanban and terminal had independent timeout budgets.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

When the dispatcher spawns a worker for a task with `max_runtime_seconds`, raise the worker subprocess's `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT` and `TERMINAL_MAX_FOREGROUND_TIMEOUT` to `max_runtime_seconds - 30s`, but only if the existing values are lower.

This keeps the fix scoped:

- No global config changes.
- No terminal tool dependency on Kanban internals.
- No behavior change for uncapped Kanban tasks.
- No lowering of explicit user terminal timeout settings.
- The worker still has a grace window to handle terminal timeout before dispatcher-enforced worker timeout.

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Voice/read-aloud platform adapters can't customize auto-TTS text prep without forking the auto-TTS pipeline

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Description

`gateway/platforms/base.py::BasePlatformAdapter._process_message_background` strips a fixed set of markdown sigils inline before sending text to TTS:

```python
speech_text = re.sub(r'[*_`#\[\]()]', '', text_content)[:4000].strip()
```

That default is fine for text-bubble platforms (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, IRC, Mattermost, BlueBubbles, Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom, WhatsApp, Signal, etc.) — strips formatting, keeps everything else.

It is wrong for voice-output adapters (LiveKit, Twilio Voice, telephony bridges, etc.), which need to drop URLs, file paths, fenced code blocks, inline code, and `MEDIA:` tags before synthesis — otherwise TTS reads `h-t-t-p-s colon slash slash docs dot example dot com…` aloud.

## Current options (neither is good)

1. **Duplicate the entire auto-TTS pipeline inside `handle_response`** — ~80 lines of fragile copy-paste (`extract_media`, `extract_images`, `extract_local_files`, attachment routing, auto-TTS gate, error handling, playback ordering) that rots whenever the base flow changes.
2. **Live with TTS speaking URLs and code blocks aloud.**

## Proposed fix

PR #26134 — extract the inline strip into a 7-line overridable method `prepare_tts_text(text)`. Default body is byte-identical to the previous inline expression, so every existing adapter sees zero behavior change. Voice adapters override it.

## Example consumer

[kortexa-ai/hermes-livekit](https://github.com/kortexa-ai/hermes-livekit) — a LiveKit WebRTC voice gateway plugin. Its `prepare_tts_text` override additionally strips code/URLs/paths/`MEDIA:` tags before synthesis while keeping the full original text on the data channel for visual rendering. That hook is the one piece of the LiveKit adapter that cannot live entirely in a plugin against today's `register_platform()` surface.

## Risk

~zero. Default behavior unchanged for all non-overriding adapters.

items.title: [Bug]: dashboard /api/status reports gateway 'stopped' on Docker (PID-1) deployment — companion to #4776

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

`dashboard /api/status` reports `gateway_running: false` / `gateway_state: "stopped"` / `gateway_pid: null` when Hermes runs as the container entrypoint in Docker/Kubernetes (PID-1 pattern), **even though the gateway is fully functional**: `hermes status` CLI correctly reports `✓ running` / `docker (foreground)`, cron jobs deliver, platform handlers (Feishu/Telegram/etc.) connect, and request handling works.

This is the **dashboard counterpart** to #4776 (CLI status path). PR #4792 was auto-closed by `hermes-sweeper` on the grounds that the CLI path was already refactored upstream into `hermes_cli.gateway.get_gateway_runtime_snapshot()` with `is_container()` detection — that is correct for the CLI, but the dashboard's `/api/status` handler in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` takes a **different code path** that still calls `gateway.status.get_running_pid()` (lock/pidfile-based), which the refactor did not touch. The sweeper review missed this case.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes via Docker with the standard image (v0.13.0 / `2026.5.7`):
   ```yaml
   command: ["gateway", "run"]
   environment:
     HERMES_DASHBOARD: "1"
     HERMES_DASHBOARD_HOST: 0.0.0.0
     HERMES_DASHBOARD_PORT: "9119"
   ```
2. Wait for the container to become healthy.
3. Confirm gateway is alive:
   ```
   $ docker exec hermes-agent hermes status
   ◆ Gateway Service
     Status:       ✓ running
     Manager:      docker (foreground)
     PID(s):       7
   ```
4. Hit dashboard:
   ```
   $ curl http://127.0.0.1:9119/api/status
   {"version":"0.13.0","gateway_running":false,"gateway_pid":null,
    "gateway_state":"stopped","gateway_platforms":{},...}
   ```

### Expected Behavior

`/api/status` should report `gateway_running: true` / `gateway_state: "running"` whenever a `hermes gateway run` process is alive in the container — consistent with what `hermes status` CLI reports.

### Actual Behavior

Always reports `stopped`. Affects every dashboard consumer: TUI dashboard widgets, status badge, anything polling `/api/status`.

### Root Cause (verified)

`hermes_cli/web_server.py:537-545` `/api/status` handler:

```python
gateway_pid = get_running_pid()       # from gateway.status — depends on pid/lock files
gateway_running = gateway_pid is not None
```

`gateway.status.get_running_pid()` first checks `is_gateway_runtime_lock_active()`, which depends on `gateway.pid` + `gateway.lock` being present. In the PID-1 entrypoint pattern these files are never reliably written (the fcntl lock fd is released after startup; the pidfile is then cleaned up by `_cleanup_invalid_pid_path`). So `get_running_pid()` returns `None` → handler reports `stopped`.

### Affected Component

Web server (`hermes_cli/web_server.py`, line ~537)

### Environment

- Hermes v0.13.0 (`2026.5.7`)
- Linux container (Debian 13.x base)
- Python 3.13.5
- `cap_drop: [ALL]` + selective adds (representative of locked-down deployments)

### Proposed Fix

Mirror PR #4792's `pgrep` fallback approach, applied to the dashboard handler. Add an `is_container()`-gated `_scan_gateway_pid_in_container()` helper invoked when the local pid/lock check returns `None`. Use `pgrep -f "hermes gateway run"` for the candidate list, then re-validate each PID via `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` argv tokens (must contain `gateway` and `run` as independent tokens) to defend against `pgrep -f`'s substring matching accidentally hitting `python -c` debug invocations.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

## Summary

Today `complete.path` and `agent/context_references.py` hardcode the six `@`-prefixes (`@diff`, `@staged`, `@file:`, `@folder:`, `@url:`, `@git:`). I'd like to propose a plugin API that lets plugins register new prefixes, mirroring how skills already extend `/` slash commands.

Filing this as an issue first to check design interest before writing a PR.

## Motivation

There's a recurring shape across workspace integrations: `@<entity-kind>:<id>` resolving to injected prompt content, paired with an autocomplete picker that searches the integration's backend. Concrete examples across different categories of plugin:

- **Issue trackers** — `@issue:ENG-123`, `@pr:456`
- **Team chat** — `@channel:platform`, `@thread:T0789...`, `@dm:alice`
- **Docs / wikis** — `@page:Q2-okr`, `@doc:design-review`
- **Local Hermes bundles** — `@task:42` (the existing Kanban plugin), `@memory:user/work`
- **Observability** — `@trace:abc123`, `@incident:INC-7`

Today every plugin that wants this either (a) ships its own input UI bypassing Hermes's TUI / web composer, or (b) asks users to `@file:/some/exported/path.txt` and pre-export — both lose the in-context picker that makes `@` valuable in the first place.

## Current state

Two coupled but separate code paths that would need to extend:

| Concern | Location | How it's wired today |
|---|---|---|
| Autocomplete | `tui_gateway/server.py:4871` `@method("complete.path")` | Hardcoded literal list of 6 prefixes at lines 4883–4889 |
| Expansion at prompt-submit | `agent/context_references.py:206` `_expand_reference()` | `REFERENCE_PATTERN` regex enumerates 6 prefixes; `if ref.kind == ...` ladder dispatches |

For comparison: slash commands already extend cleanly via `SlashCommandCompleter(skill_commands_provider=get_skill_commands)` and `PluginContext.register_command()` — there's an established pattern in this codebase.

## Rough shape (illustrative, not a proposal)

A two-half contract — autocomplete + expand — registered via `PluginContext` the same way `register_context_engine` works today. Roughly:

```python
class ContextReferenceProvider(ABC):
    prefix: str                 # "issue", "channel", "doc", ...
    description: str            # for the @-picker meta column

    async def autocomplete(self, query: str, *, limit: int) -> list[ContextCompletionItem]: ...
    async def expand(self, target: str) -> ContextExpansion | None: ...
```

Built-in prefixes would stay non-pluggable (reserved at registration). Plugin output flows through the existing 25%/50% token-limit guards in `context_references.py:167-186` unchanged. Happy to iterate on the actual shape during PR review — the sketch is just to make "what this looks like" concrete.

## Question for maintainers

**Is this direction welcome?** Or is there a reason `@` is intentionally kept minimal/closed (trust boundaries with plugin-supplied content, scope concerns, etc.) that I'm not seeing? If the answer is yes, I'll prototype a PR and we can hash out the details there.

## Out of scope (for this issue)

- Specific provider implementations — those live in individual plugins, not in core
- Frontend UI changes beyond what `complete.path` already powers — TUI / web composer reuse the same RPC
- Removing or changing semantics of any built-in prefix

items.body:
## Bug Description

`hermes gateway restart` on macOS (launchd) can leave the gateway in a stopped state instead of restarting it. The service definition gets unloaded from launchd during the restart sequence, but if the gateway process takes too long to shut down cleanly, launchd finishes unloading before the process dies — leaving the job definition removed and the gateway not running.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the gateway as a launchd service: `hermes gateway install`
2. Start an active conversation through any platform (e.g., Telegram)
3. While the agent is mid-response or mid-tool-call, run `hermes gateway restart`
4. Run `hermes gateway status` — it shows "Gateway service is not loaded"

Not 100% reproducible; it's a race between launchd unloading the job and the process exiting. It's more likely to trigger when the gateway is in the middle of processing (tool calls, LLM response in flight).

## Root Cause

Two factors combine:

**1. Race condition in the restart sequence.** `hermes gateway restart` unloads the launchd job, sends SIGTERM, then attempts to reload. If the process takes more than a few seconds to exit (e.g., it's notifying active platform sessions, flushing state), launchd may have already removed the job definition by the time the reload is attempted. The startup then fails with "Could not find service... in domain for user gui" and the gateway stays dead.

**2. KeepAlive won't rescue this.** The generated launchd plist has `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit: false` — this is correct for the normal stop case (intentional stop should stay stopped), but it means that when the restart command orchestrates a clean shutdown (exit 0), launchd correctly does NOT auto-restart the process.

From the logs, a typical failure timeline:

```
00:07:44  Stopping gateway for restart...
00:07:44  Sent shutdown notification to active chat
00:08:02  Received SIGTERM — initiating shutdown  (18s later, still running)
00:08:12  Received SIGTERM — initiating shutdown  (28s later, second signal)
          → Process finally exits (exit 0)
          → launchd: clean exit, KeepAlive won't restart
          → Job definition unloaded during restart sequence
          → Gateway stays dead until manual `hermes gateway start`
```

## Expected Behavior

`hermes gateway restart` should reliably restart the gateway on macOS, even when the process takes time to shut down gracefully.

## Actual Behavior

The gateway can end up in a "not loaded" state requiring manual `hermes gateway start` to recover.

## Workaround

```bash
hermes gateway stop && sleep 5 && hermes gateway start
```

The sleep gives launchd time to fully unload the job before the start command tries to reload it.

## Suggested Fix

The `hermes gateway restart` command should:

1. Stop the service
2. **Poll/wait** for the process to actually exit (or launchd to confirm the job is unloaded) before proceeding
3. Only then start the service

Alternatively, use `launchctl kickstart` or a similar approach instead of stop-then-start for the restart operation.

For the plist, consider `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit: true` or adding a `ThrottleInterval` so launchd handles transient failures itself — though this would need to be balanced against the desired behavior for intentional stops.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.x (Sequoia)
- Hermes version: 0.13.0
- Gateway platform: Telegram
- Service manager: launchd (user domain)

items.body:
# Feature Request: Mouse-Aware Input + Clickable Output + Smart Arrow Keys

## Summary

Three terminal UX enhancements inspired by Claude Code's terminal experience:

1. **Mouse click to position cursor in the input field ("click anywhere, edit anywhere")
2. **Clickable file paths and references** in tool output area
3. **Smart arrow key behavior** (dual-mode Up/Down)

---

## 1. Mouse-Aware Input Field (Primary)

### Problem

When typing a long command or message in Hermes' input prompt, users must hold ←/→ to move the cursor character by character to reach the middle of the text for editing. For long inputs (API queries, multi-line prompts, code snippets), this is extremely tedious and slow.

### Desired Behavior

**Mouse click anywhere in the input field should place the cursor at that position immediately.**

Example workflow:
1. User types a long command: `Can you modify the authentication middleware and also update the Prisma schema for the user model and...`
2. User realizes "middleware" should be "middleware and logging"
3. User clicks with the mouse on the word "middleware" in the input
4. Cursor jumps directly there — no need to hold ← for seconds
5. User edits and continues

### Why This Matters

| Without (current) | With (feature) |
|------------------|----------------|
| Hold ← for 5-10 seconds to reach middle of long input | Click once on the target word |
| Hard to precisely target when the input wraps to multiple lines | Click anywhere on any line |
| Error-prone counting of character positions | Visual placement, "what you see is what you edit" |
| Frustrating for Chinese/Japanese input where IME context is easily lost | Quick cursor positioning preserves IME flow |

### Implementation Notes

- Hermes CLI already uses **prompt_toolkit** for input handling
- prompt_toolkit has built-in `mouse_support=True` option that enables click-to-position on the input buffer
- This is a **one-line config toggle** in `cli.py` where the prompt session is created
- No additional dependencies required — prompt_toolkit handles mouse events natively via terminal escape sequences (SGR mouse mode `\x1b[?1000h` / `\x1b[?1002h`)
- Should be **opt-out** (enabled by default), not opt-in

### Reference

```python
from prompt_toolkit import PromptSession

session = PromptSession(mouse_support=True)  # ← this is the key line
```

prompt_toolkit's `mouse_support` enables:
- Click to position cursor in the input buffer
- The handler is built-in, already tested, and widely used (ipython, pgcli, etc.)
- Works on macOS Terminal, iTerm2, Kitty, Alacritty, Windows Terminal, and all major terminal emulators

---

## 2. Clickable Text in TUI Output Area

### Problem

When Hermes outputs file paths (e.g., from `read_file`, `search_files`, or patch diffs), they are plain text. Users cannot click on them to open the file in an editor or navigate to the referenced line.

### Desired Behavior

File paths, line references (`path/to/file.ts:42`), and URLs in Hermes' TUI output should be rendered as **clickable interactive elements**. When clicked:

- **File path** → opens in `$EDITOR` at the cursor position
- **`file.ts:42`** → opens file at line 42
- **URL** → opens in browser

### Implementation Notes

- Uses Ink (React for CLI) `<Text>` components with click handlers
- Enables SGR mouse mode in the TUI terminal
- Output paths are wrapped in clickable `<Link>`-like components
- Reference: Claude Code's implementation of clickable file paths in its TUI
- This is **separate** from Feature 1 — Feature 1 is prompt_toolkit input layer, Feature 2 is Ink TUI output rendering

---

## 3. Smart Arrow Key Behavior

### Problem

Standard terminal Up/Down arrows only have one function: history recall. Users frequently need to jump to start/end of line, but Home/End keys are on a separate key cluster, requiring hand movement.

### Desired Behavior

**Up Arrow (↑):**
| Press | Action |
|-------|--------|
| 1st press on non-empty line (cursor not at start) | Jump cursor to **beginning of current line** |
| 2nd press (already at line start) | Recall **previous command** from history |
| Already at line start | Recall previous command (normal behavior) |

**Down Arrow (↓):**
| Press | Action |
|-------|--------|
| 1st press on non-empty line (cursor not at end) | Jump cursor to **end of current line** |
| 2nd press (already at line end) | Recall **next command** from history |
| Already at line end | Recall next command (normal behavior) |

### Rationale

- Reduces hand movement between arrow keys and Home/End cluster
- Common editing pattern: type a command → tap ↑ to go back and edit → tap ↑ again to get previous command
- Non-destructive: first press always stays on the same line, only changes cursor position
- Power users (Vim/Emacs) already expect dual-mode keys
- Together with Feature 1 (mouse click), this completes the "convenient text editing" workflow

---

## Additional Context

- **Terminal input layer:** prompt_toolkit (already used by Hermes CLI)
- **TUI rendering:** Ink (React for CLI) in `ui-tui/` directory
- **Mouse mode:** Requires SGR mouse protocol `\x1b[?1000h` / `\x1b[?1002h` for click events
- **Scope:** CLI TUI mode only, not gateway/messaging platforms
- **Priority:** Feature 1 (input field click) is the highest-impact, lowest-effort improvement
- **Warning:** Feature 2 (output clickable) and Feature 3 (smart arrows) may conflict with existing prompt_toolkit mouse handlers — careful separation between input layer and output layer is needed

labels.name: comp/agent

items.body:
## Bug description

When Hermes workers use `model.openai_runtime: codex_app_server`, Kanban-dispatched tasks can complete their actual work but fail the board handoff because Codex's workspace sandbox cannot write the Kanban SQLite DB outside the task workspace.

Observed result: the worker prints a successful final answer in its task log, but `kanban_complete` / `kanban_block` cannot update the board DB, so the dispatcher later marks the task `crashed` / `blocked`.

This is a sandbox integration issue, not a domain-task failure.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 / Linux
- Codex CLI: `codex-cli 0.130.0`
- Hermes runtime: `model.openai_runtime: codex_app_server`
- Worker profiles tested: `backend-worker`, `frontend-worker`, `fullstack-worker`
- Sandbox: Bubblewrap/AppArmor working; profile configs use `default_permissions = ":workspace"`

## Reproduction shape

1. Configure worker profiles to use Codex app-server runtime.
2. Ensure direct profile smoke passes:
   ```bash
   hermes -p backend-worker chat -q 'Run a harmless shell command and reply ok' --yolo -Q
   ```
3. Create a disposable Kanban board and a scratch task assigned to a Codex-runtime worker:
   ```bash
   BOARD=codex-runtime-orchestration-smoke
   hermes kanban boards create "$BOARD" --switch || hermes kanban boards switch "$BOARD"
   hermes kanban --board "$BOARD" create "Smoke backend-worker Codex app-server runtime via Kanban" \
     --assignee backend-worker \
     --workspace scratch \
     --priority 100 \
     --max-runtime 5m \
     --max-retries 1 \
     --body "Smoke only. Print CODEX_HOME and pwd, then call kanban_complete with summary 'backend-worker codex runtime smoke ok'. If that fails, call kanban_block with exact reason."
   hermes kanban --board "$BOARD" dispatch --max 1
   ```
4. Poll / inspect:
   ```bash
   hermes kanban --board "$BOARD" list
   hermes kanban --board "$BOARD" show <task_id>
   hermes kanban --board "$BOARD" runs <task_id>
   hermes kanban --board "$BOARD" log <task_id>
   ```

## Actual behavior

Worker logs show the underlying smoke succeeded, e.g. `CODEX_HOME` and `pwd` printed correctly. But the handoff fails because the sandbox cannot write the board DB:

```text
Blocked: sqlite3 could not open the kanban database for writing from this sandbox
...
unable to open database file
```

or:

```text
The smoke check passed ...
I could not mark the Kanban task complete because writing to the board database failed under the sandbox
```

Dispatcher then records the run as `crashed` / `blocked`, even though the task itself completed.

## Expected behavior

A Kanban worker running on Codex app-server should be able to:

- keep Codex sandboxing enabled,
- execute inside its assigned scratch/worktree workspace,
- call Hermes MCP callback tools like `kanban_complete` / `kanban_block`, and
- write only the current board DB/handoff path needed for task lifecycle updates.

It should not require `danger-full-access` or `:danger-no-sandbox`.

## Proposed fix

When spawning `codex app-server` for a dispatcher-spawned worker (`HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` present), pass narrow Codex config overrides:

```python
if HERMES_KANBAN_TASK:
    board_dir = dirname(HERMES_KANBAN_DB)
    codex app-server \
      -c 'sandbox_mode="workspace-write"' \
      -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=["<board_dir>"]' \
      -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=false'
```

Why board dir rather than all of `~/.hermes/kanban`:

- `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` is already pinned by the dispatcher to the current board.
- Per-board directory is the minimal writable root needed for SQLite `kanban.db`, journals/WAL files, logs/events if needed.
- It preserves board isolation and avoids giving workers write access to unrelated boards or the whole Hermes home.

Security posture:

- sandbox remains enabled (`workspace-write`),
- no `danger-full-access`,
- no `:danger-no-sandbox`,
- no network by default,
- only the current board directory becomes an extra writable root.

## Validation performed locally

After applying the narrow writable-root bridge locally:

- Direct worker runtime smoke passed for all workers.
- MCP callback smoke passed (`web_extract` via Codex runtime).
- Real Kanban dispatcher smoke passed on a disposable board:
  - `backend-worker`: task reached `done`
  - `frontend-worker`: task reached `done`
  - `fullstack-worker`: task reached `done`
- Targeted tests passed:
  ```text
  80 passed in 4.76s
  ```
  for:
  ```bash
  python -m pytest tests/agent/transports/test_codex_app_server_runtime.py tests/agent/transports/test_codex_app_server_session.py -q
  ```

Local patch touched:

- `agent/transports/codex_app_server.py`
- `tests/agent/transports/test_codex_app_server_runtime.py`
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/codex-app-server-runtime.md`

Happy to open a PR with this patch if maintainers agree with the writable-root approach.

items.title: Telegram tool progress should roll over before message limit
items.body:
## Bug Description

On Telegram, when gateway tool progress is configured to show every tool call (`display.tool_progress: all`), a long-running turn can fill the first progress message. Once the accumulated progress text approaches Telegram's 4096 UTF-16 code unit limit, subsequent progress updates can degrade into a trail of new one-line messages instead of starting a second progress bubble and editing that one.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable Telegram gateway tool progress with `display.tool_progress: all`.
2. Run an agent task that emits many `tool.started` events in one turn.
3. Let the accumulated tool-progress text exceed Telegram's single-message limit.

## Expected Behavior

When the current progress bubble is full, the gateway should:

1. Stop editing the full first bubble.
2. Send a second progress bubble.
3. Continue editing the newest progress bubble with later tool lines.

## Actual Behavior

The gateway keeps a single historical `progress_lines` buffer and keeps trying to edit the original progress message with the full transcript. The Telegram adapter's oversized-edit path can split the edit into continuation messages, but because the progress loop does not roll over to a new current editable bubble, each later update can create another fresh continuation/message.

## Notes

The bug appears to be in `gateway/run.py::send_progress_messages()`, not in Telegram's `edit_message()` overflow handling itself. The adapter already has a split-and-deliver fallback for oversized edits; the progress loop needs to avoid sending oversized edits for live tool-progress updates by rolling over before the platform limit.

## Environment

- Platform: Telegram gateway
- Setting: `display.tool_progress: all`
- Component: `gateway/run.py`, Telegram progress message editing

labels.name: comp/agent

items.body:
## Problem

When communicating via IM platforms (especially Feishu/Lark, but also Telegram, Discord, etc.), Hermes generates responses in standard Markdown as if it's speaking in the terminal/TUI. The delivery platform then strips or misrenders the formatting.

### What it looks like on Feishu

- `**bold text**` displays as literal characters, not rendered bold
- Backtick code blocks have no background coloring
- Tables collapse into unreadable single-line text
- CJK characters produce misaligned tables because `.length()` doesn't account for wide characters
- Links don't auto-expand

### Current state of patches across platforms

Each platform has received individual band-aids:

| Platform | Fix | PR |
|----------|-----|----|
| Feishu | Force text mode for Markdown tables | #20275 (by @WuTianyi123) |
| Telegram | MarkdownV2 with strikethrough/spoiler/blockquotes | #2199, #2200 |
| Feishu (us) | Custom `md2feishu` conversion script (user-side workaround) | — |

These are **point fixes**, not an architectural solution. Hermes still generates content assuming terminal rendering, then relies on the platform adapter to patch it up.

## Root cause

The agent has **no awareness of the delivery medium** when generating responses:

```
model → generates standard Markdown (assuming TUI/terminal rendering)
                          ↓
              Feishu gateway → plain text (Markdown stripped)
                          ↓
              user sees raw Markdown syntax
```

There is no "delivery context" in the generation pipeline. The model doesn't know whether the output will go to:
- A **TUI/CLI** (full Markdown rendering)
- **Feishu** (plain text, rich media via 
- **Telegram** (MarkdownV2 subset)
- **Discord** (limited Markdown, code blocks)
- **Email** (HTML)
- **SMS** (no formatting at all)

## Desired behavior

The generation pipeline should be aware of the target platform's rendering capabilities so it can adapt output format accordingly.

**Three possible levels of solution** (any would be an improvement):

### Level 1: Format layer (simplest, lowest risk)
A per-platform output formatter that post-processes standard Markdown into platform-optimized text before delivery. The model generates in standard Markdown, the pipeline applies the right formatter. Example: for Feishu, convert `|table|` syntax to aligned text with separator lines, convert `**bold**` to `【bold】`.

### Level 2: Context injection
Inject the delivery platform into the system prompt so the model can adapt during generation. For example: "You are speaking on Feishu Bot — do not rely on Markdown table syntax; use aligned text instead." This requires no code change but depends on the model following the instruction (works better with pro models).

### Level 3: Adapter protocol (most thorough)
A unified output capability descriptor per platform. Each platform adapter declares what formatting it supports (Markdown full / subset / plain text / HTML). The generation layer or the model adapts accordingly. This would also benefit new platforms — add the descriptor, get correct formatting automatically.

## Current workaround (user-side)

We maintain a custom `md2feishu` skill that converts Markdown to Feishu-friendly text:

- Tables → aligned text with `┌┬┐` separator lines (CJK-width aware)
- `##` headings → `text + ──` line
- `**bold**` → `【bold】`
- Blockquotes → `▎ prefix`
- Links → expanded with URL shown

This works but has two fundamental problems:
1. Must be **explicitly invoked** — the model doesn't auto-detect when to use it
2. It's a **user-side patch**, not a platform capability — every Hermes user on Feishu has to invent their own

## Related

- #20275 — Force text mode for Feishu markdown tables (partial fix, Level 0)
- Telegram MarkdownV2 support (#2199, #2200) — another partial fix

## Environment

- Hermes version: v2026.5.7 (v0.13.0)
- Primary affected platform: Feishu/Lark Bot
- Also affects: Telegram (partial), Discord (partial), any plain-text gateway

## Labels
labels: ["enhancement", "ux", "platform/feishu"]

Migrate the FAL backend out of `tools/image_generation_tool.py` and into `plugins/image_gen/fal/`, matching the architecture established by PR #25182 (web), PR #25214 (browser), and the existing image_gen plugins (OpenAI, xAI, openai-codex). After this lands, `TOOL_CATEGORIES["image_gen"]["providers"]` drops to zero hardcoded rows — same shape as `video_gen`.

This is the explicit follow-up referenced in `hermes_cli/tools_config.py::_plugin_image_gen_providers`:

> "FAL is skipped — it's already exposed by the hardcoded `TOOL_CATEGORIES["image_gen"]` entries. **When FAL gets ported to a plugin in a follow-up PR**, the hardcoded entries go away and this function surfaces it alongside OpenAI automatically."

## Current state (what to migrate)

**Backend code** — all in `tools/image_generation_tool.py` (~700 LoC of FAL-specific surface):

- **18-model catalog** (`_MODELS` dict at line ~140-323): `fal-ai/flux-2/klein/9b` (default), `fal-ai/flux-pro/v1.1`, `fal-ai/recraft-v3`, `fal-ai/imagen4/preview`, etc. — each with per-model `default_aspect_ratio`, `default_quality`, `default_steps`, etc.
- **`DEFAULT_MODEL = "fal-ai/flux-2/klein/9b"`** (line 326)
- **Managed Nous gateway integration** (lines ~352-471):
  - `_resolve_managed_fal_gateway()` — consults `resolve_managed_tool_gateway("fal-queue")`
  - `_ManagedFalSyncClient` — wraps `fal_client.SyncClient` for Nous-subscription users with idempotency-key handling
  - `_get_managed_fal_client()` + `_managed_fal_client` + `_managed_fal_client_config` + lock
- **Direct FAL SDK path** — `_submit_fal_request()` (line ~472) dispatches between managed + direct
- **Payload builder** — `_build_fal_payload()` (line ~561) — model-specific knob mapping
- **Built-in upscaler** — `_upscale_image()` via `fal-ai/clarity-upscaler` (line ~607); fires after `image_generate_tool` succeeds when the per-model spec says `upscale: True`
- **Resolution helpers** — `_resolve_fal_model()`, `_read_configured_image_model()`, `_extract_http_status()`
- **`check_fal_api_key()`** — reaches into both gateway state + `FAL_KEY` env var

**Dispatcher** — `_dispatch_to_plugin_provider()` at `image_generation_tool.py:993` explicitly skips FAL:

```python
if not configured or configured == "fal":
    return None  # fall through to in-tree FAL path
```

**Picker** — `_plugin_image_gen_providers()` in `hermes_cli/tools_config.py:1467-1470` skips FAL because it's surfaced via the hardcoded `TOOL_CATEGORIES["image_gen"]["providers"]` entries.

## Why this is bigger than #25214 looked

Three things that don't apply to the browser migration:

1. **FAL is the default backend.** Browser providers are all opt-in via explicit `browser.cloud_provider`. FAL fires whenever `image_gen.provider` is unset OR explicitly set to `"fal"`. The plugin needs to participate cleanly in both code paths — including the no-config fall-through that `_dispatch_to_plugin_provider` currently skips.

2. **Managed Nous gateway plumbing.** Browser providers manage their own credentials end-to-end. FAL has a gateway-vs-direct selection inside the provider AND `check_image_generation_requirements()` consults the gateway state for the requirements check. The plugin needs to either inherit the gateway code or call back into a shared helper.

3. **video_gen FAL plugin already exists** at `plugins/video_gen/fal/__init__.py` with its own `_load_fal_client` lazy-import + direct `fal_client.subscribe()` calls. It does NOT have managed-gateway support today — it's direct-only. Image-gen FAL should likely share the `fal_client` plumbing with video_gen rather than each plugin re-implementing it. Right ordering is:

   a. Factor out `tools/fal_common.py` (lazy `fal_client` load, managed-gateway resolution, `_ManagedFalSyncClient`, `_submit_fal_request`).
   b. Migrate image_gen FAL → `plugins/image_gen/fal/` consuming `tools.fal_common`.
   c. Refactor `plugins/video_gen/fal/__init__.py` to consume the same `tools.fal_common` (drops its inline `_load_fal_client` duplicate).
   d. (Optional) Add managed-gateway support to video_gen FAL while we're in there.

## What "applying the #25214 template" means concretely

### Step 1 — factor shared FAL plumbing into `tools/fal_common.py`

Move these out of `tools/image_generation_tool.py` (keep as re-export shims for backward compat with patched tests):

- `_load_fal_client()` + `fal_client` placeholder
- `_resolve_managed_fal_gateway()`
- `_normalize_fal_queue_url_format()`
- `_ManagedFalSyncClient`
- `_get_managed_fal_client()` + `_managed_fal_client` global + lock
- `_submit_fal_request()`
- `_extract_http_status()`

`tests/tools/test_managed_media_gateways.py` (~298 LoC) already patches these names — preserve them via re-exports per the `in-tree-to-plugin-migration` skill's "re-export shims" pattern.

### Step 2 — refactor `plugins/video_gen/fal/__init__.py` to use `tools.fal_common`

Drops the inline `_load_fal_client` + `_fal_client` global. Behaves identically. (Bonus: opens the door to managed-gateway support in a future PR.)

### Step 3 — new `plugins/image_gen/fal/{plugin.yaml,__init__.py}`

Mirrors `plugins/image_gen/openai/__init__.py` structure (single-file ABC impl + `register()`):

```python
class FalImageGenProvider(ImageGenProvider):
    @property
    def name(self) -> str: return "fal"

    @property
    def display_name(self) -> str: return "FAL"

    def is_available(self) -> bool:
        # FAL_KEY direct OR Nous managed gateway both count
        return check_fal_api_key()

    def list_models(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        # 18-entry catalog from _MODELS dict

    def default_model(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return "fal-ai/flux-2/klein/9b"

    def get_setup_schema(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        # Matches the existing hardcoded TOOL_CATEGORIES["image_gen"] FAL entry
        # — env_vars for FAL_KEY + Nous Subscription gating

    def generate(self, prompt, aspect_ratio="landscape", **kwargs) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        # Wraps tools.fal_common._submit_fal_request + _build_fal_payload
```

The `_MODELS` catalog moves into the plugin (it's purely FAL-specific). `_build_fal_payload`, `_resolve_fal_model` likewise — these have zero callers outside `image_generate_tool`.

### Step 4 — dispatcher cutover

Remove the `configured == "fal"` skip in `_dispatch_to_plugin_provider()`. Have `image_generate_tool()`'s no-config path also route through the registry (fetching the `"fal"` provider explicitly when nothing is configured), so the plugin handles every code path.

### Step 5 — drop the FAL skip in `_plugin_image_gen_providers()` + delete hardcoded FAL row

After Step 4, `TOOL_CATEGORIES["image_gen"]["providers"]` can drop to zero hardcoded rows — matches `video_gen`. The "Nous Subscription (Managed FAL)" UX row stays as a non-provider setup-flow entry, same shape as the browser migration kept "Nous Subscription (Browser Use cloud)".

### Step 6 — keep `_upscale_image()` in `tools/image_generation_tool.py`

The upscaler currently fires *after* `image_generate_tool` succeeds when the model spec has `upscale: True`. It's a wrapper concern, not a backend concern. Stays in the tool wrapper, calls back into FAL via the plugin (or `tools.fal_common._submit_fal_request` directly — same difference).

### Step 7 — tests

- Add `tests/plugins/image_gen/test_fal_provider.py` (~150 LoC mirroring `test_openai_provider.py` / `test_xai_provider.py`)
- Existing `tests/tools/test_image_generation*.py` tests keep working unchanged because the patched names are still importable from `tools.image_generation_tool` (re-export shims)
- Behavior-parity subprocess sweep mirroring `tests/plugins/browser/check_parity_vs_main.py`:
  - `image_gen.provider` unset → resolves to FAL (default)
  - `image_gen.provider: fal` explicit → resolves to FAL (via registry)
  - `image_gen.provider: openai` → resolves to OpenAI plugin (no regression)
  - `image_gen.provider: <typo>` → falls back to FAL default (preserves legacy)
  - With Nous managed gateway configured + no FAL_KEY → still resolves
  - With FAL_KEY + `tool_gateway.image_gen: gateway` → managed wins

## Out of scope

- **`_upscale_image` becoming pluggable.** It's coupled to the model catalog (per-model `upscale: bool` knob). Could be its own plugin category in the future but not in scope here.
- **video_gen FAL gaining managed-gateway support.** Could land in the same PR if it's clean, but file as a separate issue if it adds complexity.
- **Migrating the 18-model catalog format.** The catalog stays as a dict literal in the plugin; restructuring into `ImageGenProvider.list_models()` entries with first-class typing is out of scope.

## Architectural parity payoff

After this, all four pluggable-backend subsystems work identically:

- `plugins/web/<vendor>/` ↔ `plugins/browser/<vendor>/` ↔ `plugins/image_gen/<vendor>/` ↔ `plugins/video_gen/<vendor>/`

And both FAL-using plugins share `tools/fal_common.py` instead of each re-implementing the `fal_client` lazy-load.

## Related

- PR #25182 — web-provider plugin migration (the reference template)
- PR #25214 / #25580 — browser-provider plugin migration (closest analog)
- #14182 — tracking: `hermes_agent` package restructure (broader umbrella)

items.title: hermes codex-runtime migrate produces invalid ~/.codex/config.toml (duplicate keys, scoped default_permissions, leaked HERMES_HOME)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes codex-runtime migrate` (called automatically when switching to `codex_app_server` runtime) can produce a `~/.codex/config.toml` that codex refuses to load. Three distinct bugs combine to break the file. I hit this on my own setup and had to hand-fix the resulting `duplicate key` parse error.

The three bugs are independent and each one is fixable in isolation.

---

## Bug A — `default_permissions` lands inside the previous `[mcp_servers.X]` table

**File:** `hermes_cli/codex_runtime_plugin_migration.py` (`render_codex_toml_section`, ~lines 270–303)

The renderer emits:

```toml
# managed by hermes-agent — `hermes codex-runtime migrate` regenerates this section

default_permissions = ":workspace"

[mcp_servers.hermes-tools]
…
# end hermes-agent managed section
```

That's correct TOML **only** if no open table scope exists above it. But `~/.codex/config.toml` already contains user-owned `[mcp_servers.<name>]` tables above the managed section. When the managed block is appended (or re-rendered in place but ordered after pre-existing tables), TOML's lexer reads `default_permissions = ":workspace"` as a key of the most-recent table header (in my case `[mcp_servers.omx_team_run]`). On the next `hermes codex-runtime migrate` it re-emits the same key, codex's strict TOML parser sees a duplicate key inside that table, and the load fails:

```
failed to read configuration layers: /Users/<user>/.codex/config.toml:157:10: duplicate key
```

**Fix sketch:** emit `default_permissions` either (a) at the *very top* of the file (above any pre-existing tables) before any user table opens, or (b) wrap it in a deliberate `[]` or `[hermes]` table header so its scope is unambiguous, or (c) keep using top-level but write `default_permissions` BEFORE we append anything else to the file, ensuring it precedes the first table header. Option (c) is least invasive but requires reading + rewriting the file rather than appending.

---

## Bug B — `[plugins."<name>@<marketplace>"]` tables get duplicated

**File:** `hermes_cli/codex_runtime_plugin_migration.py` (`_strip_existing_managed_block` lines ~307–350, `_query_codex_plugins` ~353–410)

`_strip_existing_managed_block` removes content **only between** the `MIGRATION_MARKER` and `MIGRATION_END_MARKER` lines. Plugins that codex itself manages (e.g. installed via `codex plugins enable …` directly, before hermes ran) live OUTSIDE the markers — they were written by codex, not by us.

When `migrate()` runs:
1. `_query_codex_plugins()` calls the live codex app-server and gets the list of installed plugins (including the ones codex added itself).
2. `render_codex_toml_section()` emits a fresh `[plugins."<name>@<marketplace>"] enabled = true` for each.
3. The new block is appended below the existing codex-managed `[plugins.X]` tables that we never stripped.

Result: 5 plugins in my file each have two `[plugins."<name>@<marketplace>"]` entries — one codex put there, one we put there. TOML rejects the duplicate-table-header.

**Fix sketch:** before re-emitting `[plugins.X]` blocks, scan the un-managed portion of the file and skip any plugin whose `name@marketplace` already exists there. Or: own the `[plugins.*]` namespace entirely (strip ALL `[plugins.*]` tables from the file before re-rendering), since codex's `plugin/list` returns them anyway.

---

## Bug C — `HERMES_HOME` from `os.environ` leaks into the user's real `~/.codex/config.toml`

**File:** `hermes_cli/codex_runtime_plugin_migration.py` (`_build_hermes_tools_entry`, lines ~445–450)

```python
hermes_home = os.environ.get("HERMES_HOME")
if hermes_home:
    env["HERMES_HOME"] = hermes_home
```

This reads `HERMES_HOME` from the calling process's environment at migrate-time and burns it verbatim into the `[mcp_servers.hermes-tools] env = { HERMES_HOME = "…" }` line.

My `~/.codex/config.toml` had:

```toml
HERMES_HOME = "/private/var/folders/.../pytest-of-kshitij/pytest-137/popen-gw2/test_enable_succeeds_when_code0/hermes_test"
```

— a long-deleted pytest tempdir. Codex spawned the hermes-tools MCP subprocess against a path that no longer exists, so every codex-routed tool call into hermes failed silently.

This means **some test run** (either `test_enable_succeeds_when_codex_present` or a sibling under `tests/hermes_cli/test_codex_runtime_*.py`) executed `migrate()` with the real `Path.home() / ".codex"` while `monkeypatch.setenv("HERMES_HOME", str(tmp_path))` was active.

Looking at `tests/hermes_cli/test_codex_runtime_plugin_migration.py`, all the explicit test cases DO pass `codex_home=tmp_path` and don't leak. But:

- The `migrate()` default is `codex_home = codex_home or Path.home() / ".codex"` (line 509). If any caller (or future test) forgets to pass `codex_home`, it writes to the user's actual `~/.codex/`.
- `_build_hermes_tools_entry()` reads `os.environ` regardless of the `codex_home` argument. So even when `codex_home=tmp_path` is passed, an active `monkeypatch.setenv("HERMES_HOME", ...)` will produce TOML that — if it ever gets copied/merged into the user's real config — embeds the tempdir.
- The pytest test path `test_enable_succeeds_when_code0` comes from `test_enable_succeeds_when_codex_present` (pytest's path-length-truncation behavior on macOS), which is in `test_codex_runtime_switch.py` — that test patches `crs.check_codex_binary_ok` but does NOT patch `crs.crpm.migrate`, and `crs.apply()` auto-calls `migrate()` for `codex_app_server`. That migrate() call uses the real `Path.home() / ".codex"`.

**Fix sketch:**
1. Don't read `HERMES_HOME` from `os.environ` at migrate-time. Instead, derive it from `get_hermes_home()` (the canonical resolution) or omit it from the codex env entirely — the spawned hermes subprocess will resolve its own `HERMES_HOME` on startup.
2. If passthrough is genuinely needed (e.g. for non-default profile dirs), wrap the value with a sanity check: refuse to write a `HERMES_HOME` path that doesn't exist or is under a `pytest-of-*` ancestor.
3. In `crs.apply()`, gate the auto-`migrate()` call so it's skipped during tests — e.g. unconditionally `patch("hermes_cli.codex_runtime_plugin_migration.migrate")` in the relevant `conftest.py` autouse fixture, or have `apply()` accept an injectable migrator. The current test suite mocks it in *some* cases (`test_enable_triggers_mcp_migration`, `test_disable_does_not_trigger_migration`, `test_migration_failure_does_not_block_enable`) but NOT in `test_enable_succeeds_when_codex_present` and `test_binary_check_cached_within_apply`.

---

## How I hit this

1. Was running the `tests/hermes_cli/test_codex_runtime_*.py` suite during another change.
2. `test_enable_succeeds_when_codex_present` ran `crs.apply(cfg, "codex_app_server")` with no migrate mock → real `migrate()` ran against my real `~/.codex/config.toml` with `monkeypatch.setenv("HERMES_HOME", "<pytest tempdir>")` from a sibling test active in the same worker.
3. Later, a second `migrate()` call (either from another test, or from me running `hermes codex-runtime migrate` to "fix" things) re-emitted plugin tables AND `default_permissions` — producing duplicate `[plugins.X]` table headers AND a `default_permissions =` key scoped under `[mcp_servers.omx_team_run]`.
4. Next `codex` startup hit the TOML parser duplicate-key error and refused to load.

I patched the file by hand: hoisted `default_permissions` to the top of the file, removed the duplicate `[plugins.*]` tables, and replaced the leaked pytest-tempdir `HERMES_HOME` with `/Users/kshitij/.hermes`. Codex now loads cleanly.

## Repro

```bash
# Pre-state: ~/.codex/config.toml has user-managed [mcp_servers.X] tables
#            AND codex-installed [plugins."<name>@<marketplace>"] tables outside hermes markers.

# Trigger:
hermes codex-runtime migrate   # or `hermes setup` → enable codex_app_server

# After:
codex   # fails with "duplicate key" parse error
```

Or via test suite (Bug C only):

```bash
bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_codex_runtime_switch.py::TestCodexRuntimeApply::test_enable_succeeds_when_codex_present
# then inspect ~/.codex/config.toml — HERMES_HOME points at a pytest tempdir
```

## Priority

P2 — bricks codex usage entirely after first `hermes codex-runtime migrate` for users who have existing codex-managed plugins or any pre-existing `[mcp_servers.*]` tables. Hand-fix is straightforward but the failure mode (`codex` silently refusing to start) is hostile.

## Labels

`comp/runtime`, `type/bug`, `P2`

items.title: [Feature]: Native user timezone configuration — Hermes should default to user's timezone, not UTC

labels.name: comp/agent

labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

## Problem

Hermes runs in a Docker/UTC container but users live in different timezones. Currently, every time output relies on multiple unreliable layers of workaround to display the correct timezone:

1. `TZ=Asia/Shanghai` environment variable — doesn't propagate to all cron processes
2. `SOUL.md` rules telling the model "use BJT" — works for pro models, unreliable for flash
3. Manual "(UTC+8)" annotation in every response — depends on the model remembering

This has caused recurring confusion across sessions (3+ corrections logged). The user sees UTC times and thinks the agent is reporting wrong hours, because it literally is — "3 AM" when it's 11 AM locally.

## Root cause

There is no **single, persistent, universally enforced** user timezone configuration in Hermes.

```
system clock (UTC in Docker)
    ↓
datetime.now() returns UTC
    ↓
model outputs "current time is 3:00 AM" (UTC)
    ↓
user sees wrong time — it's 11:00 AM in Beijing
```

The fix is spread across:
- Python `TZ` env var (process-level, some processes don't inherit it)
- System prompt rules (model-level, depends on model compliance)
- Manual model behavior (output-level, depends on model remembering)

None of these are guaranteed. The system needs a single source of truth.

## Desired behavior

A `display.timezone` config option (e.g., `display.timezone: Asia/Shanghai`) that is injected into **every layer** automatically:

| Layer | Current | Desired |
|-------|---------|---------|
| System prompt | SOUL.md rules (unreliable) | Config → prompt: "Use Asia/Shanghai for all times" |
| Python runtime | `TZ` env var (not inherited everywhere) | `datetime.now(tz=pytz.timezone(config.timezone))` |
| Cron display | UTC stored, model manually converts | Cron stores UTC, display layer auto-converts |
| File timestamps | `os.path.getmtime()` returns UTC float | Logs show user timezone |

This should require **zero user-side configuration** beyond adding one line to config.yaml.

## Timeline of corrections

- First occurrence: Container defaults to UTC, model reports wrong time
- Fix 1: Added `TZ=Asia/Shanghai` to `.env` and `~/.bashrc`
- Fix 2: Added "all times in BJT" rule to SOUL.md
- Fix 3: Added explicit check in cron prompts

Each fix reduced frequency but none eliminated the problem. The issue keeps recurring because the root cause (no native config) is never addressed.

## Related

- System timezone detection on agent startup
- `hermes doctor` should report configured vs system timezone
- Cron schedule display should show times in user-configured timezone

## Environment

- Container: Docker (UTC system clock)
- User timezone: Asia/Shanghai (UTC+8)
- Hermes version: v2026.5.7 (v0.13.0)
```

### Proposed Solution

Validated at startup against zoneinfo.available_timezones(). If invalid → fall back to UTC with a warning in hermes doctor.
Layer 1: System prompt (model always sees the right time)
Instead of relying on SOUL.md rules, inject the current time in the user's configured timezone directly into the system prompt at every turn:
Current time: 2026-05-15 20:30 CST (Asia/Shanghai, UTC+8)
This is generated from the config — the model sees the correct time with zero effort. No rules for the model to remember or ignore.
Layer 2: Python runtime (developer tooling)
Make the timezone-aware helpers available everywhere:
# In hermes_tools (available to execute_code, cron scripts, skills)

def now() -> datetime:

    """Current time in the user's configured timezone."""

    ...



def fmt(dt: datetime = None) -> str:

    """Format a datetime for user-facing output."""

    ...

Also set os.environ["TZ"] at gateway/CLI startup so all subprocesses (terminal, cron jobs) inherit the timezone automatically — no more env var propagation issues.
Layer 3: Cron display (user sees local time, not UTC)
Cron schedules stored as UTC internally (to avoid DST issues) but displayed to the user in their configured timezone:
# Stored internally:
"schedule": "0 23 * * *"     # UTC

# Displayed to user:
"Next run: 2026-05-16 07:00 CST (Asia/Shanghai, UTC+8)"
Validation
$ hermes doctor | grep timezone
System timezone:  UTC
Config timezone:  Asia/Shanghai  ✓
Cron display:     UTC → CST (+8h)
Why this is the right approach
Backward compatible: default is UTC, existing users see no change
Single source of truth: one config line, no env vars, no SOUL.md rules, no model remembering
Covers all layers: model, Python code, cron, logs
Low implementation cost: ~200 lines across 5 small PRs

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Feature Type

Configuration option

### Scope

None

### Debug Report (optional)

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes currently includes a basic `brave-free` web search provider. Brave also offers paid Search API, Data for Search, and grounding context capabilities that are useful for research agents: web search with extra snippets, images, news, videos, discussions, FAQ, infobox sections where available, suggestions, and grounding context data.

## Proposal

Add a first-class Brave Search API paid provider/tool so users can select it during setup, enter `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY`, and use richer modes:

- `both` default: web search plus grounding context
- `web`
- `llm` mode name for the Brave grounding context endpoint
- `images`
- `news`
- `videos`
- `discussions` where Brave returns discussions or supports an equivalent filter
- `suggest`
- optional bounded `raw` output for debugging, if appropriate

## Why

This makes Hermes more useful for research workflows and source grounding while keeping the existing free/basic Brave provider intact.

## Notes

This should not break existing `web_search` compatibility. The generic `web_search` tool can continue to return the standard `{data: {web: [...]}}` shape, while an advanced `brave_search` tool exposes the richer Brave-specific modes.
