items.body:
## Bug Description

`hermes doctor` reports Gemini as having an invalid API key, even when the key is valid and working.

```
  ✗ gemini               (invalid API key)
```

And the summary recommends:

```
  1. Check GOOGLE_API_KEY in .env
```

But the key is valid — verified manually hitting the OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```bash
curl -s "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/models" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GOOGLE_API_KEY"
# Returns HTTP 200
```

## Root Cause

The Gemini provider profile in `plugins/model-providers/gemini/__init__.py` has:

```python
gemini = GeminiProfile(
    name="gemini",
    env_vars=("GOOGLE_API_KEY", "GEMINI_API_KEY"),
    base_url="https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta",
    ...
)
```

No explicit `models_url` is set. The doctor probe in `_build_apikey_providers_list()` (`hermes_cli/doctor.py`) constructs the health-check URL from the profile base_url:

```python
_models_url = (
    (_pp.models_url or (_pp.base_url.rstrip("/") + "/models"))
    if _pp.base_url else None
)
```

This produces:

```
https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models
```

This native Gemini endpoint does **not** accept `Authorization: Bearer` — it expects the API key as a query parameter (`?key=...`). The 401 response causes doctor to report "invalid API key".

However, Hermes **never uses this endpoint in practice**. Actual Gemini API calls go through the OpenAI-compatible surface at:

```
https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai
```

which accepts Bearer auth and works correctly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a valid `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in `~/.hermes/.env` (from aistudio.google.com)
2. Run `hermes doctor`
3. Observe false positive: `✗ gemini (invalid API key)`

## Expected Behavior

The health check should probe the OpenAI-compatible endpoint that Hermes actually uses.

## Proposed Fix

**Option A — Set explicit `models_url` on the GeminiProfile:**

```python
gemini = GeminiProfile(
    name="gemini",
    ...
    base_url="https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta",
    models_url="https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/models",
)
```

**Option B — Special-case Gemini in the doctor probe** to use the `/openai/models` path instead of `/models`.

Option A is simpler and makes the intent explicit.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `main` branch (May 2026)
- Provider: ollama-launch with gemini-2.5-flash as fallback/delegation/auxiliary
- OS: Linux (Proxmox LXC)

items.body:
### Bug Description

Two interacting defaults turn an Anthropic 429 (soft rate limit) into a hard outage:

1. `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` `build_anthropic_client` (and `build_anthropic_bedrock_client`) construct `Anthropic(...)` / `AnthropicBedrock(...)` **without** setting `max_retries`, so the SDK's default `max_retries=2` kicks in. The SDK retries 429/5xx with a 1-2s exponential backoff and **ignores `Retry-After`**.
2. `run_agent.py:14462` caps `Retry-After` at 120s: `_retry_after = min(float(_ra_raw), 120)  # Cap at 2 minutes`. On Anthropic Tier 1 accounts the input-token bucket resets in ~171s.

**Net effect on a rate-limited account:**
- SDK fires 2 silent retries inside hermes's outer retry loop → burns through 2-3 request slots against a bucket that won't refill for minutes
- Outer hermes retry sleeps 120s (capped) and fires again before the actual reset window → another nested SDK retry burst
- Soft per-minute throttle escalates into hard request-count exhaustion; the agent appears hung

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Anthropic API key on Tier 1 (or any account where reset window > 120s)
2. Saturate input-token budget (long conversation / many parallel turns)
3. Receive `429` with `Retry-After: 171` (or any value > 120)
4. Observe: SDK retries fire silently inside hermes's retry, hermes sleeps 120s instead of 171s, request slots exhaust before the actual reset window

### Expected Behavior

- Single retry strategy: hermes's outer loop owns rate-limit backoff (it already reads `Retry-After`)
- `Retry-After` honored up to a sane ceiling (e.g. 600s — covers all realistic provider windows while still rejecting absurd values)

### Actual Behavior

- Two retry layers fighting each other
- 120s cap turns a 171s reset window into a death loop

### Affected Component

- Agent Core (conversation loop)

### Root Cause Analysis

Verified on `origin/main` HEAD `77276070f5` (2026-05-15):

- [`agent/anthropic_adapter.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/agent/anthropic_adapter.py) `build_anthropic_client` — no `max_retries` kwarg passed to `Anthropic(**kwargs)` → SDK default 2
- [`agent/anthropic_adapter.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/agent/anthropic_adapter.py) `build_anthropic_bedrock_client` — no `max_retries` kwarg passed to `AnthropicBedrock(...)` → SDK default 2
- [`run_agent.py:14462`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/run_agent.py#L14462) — `_retry_after = min(float(_ra_raw), 120)`

### Proposed Fix

1. Set `max_retries=0` on **both** SDK constructors (Anthropic + AnthropicBedrock) — delegate retries to hermes's outer loop entirely. The outer loop already honors `Retry-After`; the SDK layer just doubles up.
2. Raise the `Retry-After` cap from 120s to 600s (covers Anthropic Tier 1 and similar providers; still rejects pathological hours/days values).

I have working commits in my fork that survived rebase onto v2026.5.7 (tests included). Happy to open a PR — wanted to surface this first since `max_retries=0` is a behavior change for any user relying on SDK-level retry semantics.

### Environment

- Hermes: v2026.5.7 base + verified against `origin/main` 2026-05-15
- Python: 3.11+
- OS: macOS 15.x (bug is platform-independent — pure provider retry logic)

items.body:
## Problem

Hermes Agent's background self-improvement review (triggered by \`creation_nudge_interval\`) autonomously creates or updates skills in \`~/.hermes/skills/\` with no user involvement. When a skill with the same name already exists, the agent just overwrites it — the user never knows.

## Proposed Solution

Add a user-confirmation step before any \`skill_manage(action='create')\` call from the background review.

**Config option:**
```yaml
skills:
  creation_nudge_interval: 15
  creation_requires_approval: true   # default: false (current autonomous behavior)
```

**Behavior when \`creation_requires_approval: true\`:**

1. Background review detects a signal to create/update skill X
2. Before writing anything, present a diff to the user:
   - If X **does not exist** → show the proposed SKILL.md content and ask "Create this skill? [y/n]"
   - If X **already exists** → show a side-by-side diff (current vs. proposed) and ask "Skill 'X' already exists. Overwrite? [y/n / show diff]"
3. User approves → skill is written; User declines → nothing is written, review ends for this cycle

This mirrors the \`auto_detection.mode: suggest\` pattern already present in the codebase, but for **creation** rather than loading.

## Why This Matters

- **Overwrite protection**: User explicitly approves before any existing skill is modified
- **Diff visibility**: Seeing the actual content difference is far more useful than just "skill already exists" warning
- **User autonomy**: Persistent knowledge files should not be written to a user's filesystem without consent
- **Discovery**: Users become aware of what the agent is learning about their workflow

## References

- #13534 — Pre-Creation Validation (mentions this as proposal B)
- #25833 — Self-created skills lack mechanism-level guarantees
- \`auto_detection.mode: suggest\` — existing precedent

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway restart orphans in-flight delegate subagents — 12+ min timeout

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Symptom

When the gateway restarts (via `hermes gateway restart` or launchd KeepAlive), any delegate_task subagents that are in-flight are not cancelled. They become orphaned, lose their API connections, and eventually time out after 12–16 minutes of no response. The user sees:

- Agent idle timeout (781s for main agent, 757s/765s for subagents)
- Subagent interrupted mid-API-call errors
- Lost work from the delegate tasks

## Evidence

From `gateway.log` during a restart event (gateway received restart command at 06:56, old process lingered until 07:15):

```
No response from provider for 968s (model: deepseek-v4-pro, context: ~199,242 tokens)
No response from provider for 1097s (model: deepseek-v4-pro, context: ~199,242 tokens)
[subagent-0] No response from provider for 757s (model: kimi-k2.6, context: ~3,080 tokens)
[subagent-1] No response from provider for 765s (model: kimi-k2.6, context: ~5,538 tokens)
[subagent-1] Interrupted during API call.
[subagent-0] Interrupted during API call.
```

All 56 timeout/disconnect/interrupt events in the gateway log across multiple sessions occurred during gateway restart transition periods.

## Root Cause

`cancel_session_processing` in the gateway shutdown path does not recursively cancel in-flight delegate subagents. When the gateway is shutting down:

1. The main agent session gets a shutdown signal
2. But delegate_task subagents continue running independently
3. The gateway process loses its API connections during restart
4. Subagents wait indefinitely for responses (757s, 765s observed)
5. Eventually they hit connection-level timeouts and are interrupted

## Proposed Fix

In the gateway shutdown sequence, before disconnecting platform adapters:

1. Collect all active sessions with in-flight delegate tasks
2. Cancel each subagent (set interrupt flag, cancel pending API calls)
3. Wait for subagents to acknowledge cancellation (with a short grace period, e.g. 5s)
4. Only then proceed with transport disconnect and gateway shutdown

## Related

- #12029 — session leak across restart/exception paths
- #25966 — gateway restart force-kill races cleanup tail

items.title: Skill loading fails when skill is in external_dirs (absolute path rglob bug)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

When a skill is located in an external skills directory (e.g., `~/.agents/skills/`), invoking it via slash command (e.g., `/daily-ops`) fails with:

```
[Failed to load skill: daily-ops]
```

The same skill loads fine via `skill_view()` CLI or when called by bare name.

## Root Cause

In `agent/skill_commands.py`, `_load_skill_payload()` passes the `skill_dir` (absolute path) from `get_skill_commands()` to `skill_view()`:

```python
# get_skill_commands() returns:
# skill_dir: /Users/hdj/.agents/skills/daily-ops  (absolute path)

loaded = _load_skill_payload(skill_info["skill_dir"])
```

When the absolute path is outside `SKILLS_DIR` (`~/.hermes/skills/`), the fallback normalization keeps it as-is:

```python
# skill_commands.py line 63-67
if identifier_path.is_absolute():
    try:
        normalized = str(identifier_path.resolve().relative_to(SKILLS_DIR.resolve()))
    except Exception:
        normalized = raw_identifier  # ← keeps absolute path!
```

Then `skill_view()` receives this absolute path and crashes at line 1006:

```python
# skills_tool.py line 1006
for found_md in search_dir.rglob(f"{name}.md"):
    # ↑ rglob with absolute path raises NotImplementedError
```

The exception is caught by `_load_skill_payload`'s broad `except Exception`, which returns `None`, producing the `[Failed to load skill: ...]` error message.

## Reproduction

1. Configure `external_dirs` in config.yaml to include `~/.agents/skills/`
2. Place any skill (e.g., `daily-ops`) in `~/.agents/skills/daily-ops/`
3. Invoke `/daily-ops` from CLI or gateway platform
4. Observe `[Failed to load skill: daily-ops]` response

## Suggested Fix

In `agent/skill_commands.py` `_load_skill_payload()`, extract the directory name instead of keeping the absolute path:

```python
if identifier_path.is_absolute():
    try:
        normalized = str(identifier_path.resolve().relative_to(SKILLS_DIR.resolve()))
    except Exception:
        # Extract last path component as skill name instead of absolute path
        normalized = identifier_path.name
```

This ensures `skill_view()` receives a relative name (e.g., `daily-ops`) that it can properly search for.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: latest (as of 2026-05-15)
- OS: macOS 26.5
- Skills location: `~/.agents/skills/` (external_dirs)

items.title: [Bug]: cron jobs fail with 'No Anthropic credentials found' when authenticated via 'hermes auth add anthropic --type oauth' (credential_pool ignored by resolve_anthropic_token)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Summary

`resolve_anthropic_token()` in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py:945` does not consult the **credential_pool** (`~/.hermes/auth.json`) when resolving Anthropic OAuth credentials. As a result, cron jobs that route through `runtime_provider.resolve_runtime_provider()` fail with `AuthError: No Anthropic credentials found` even when `hermes auth add anthropic --type oauth` (PKCE) has been completed and `hermes auth status anthropic` reports `logged in`.

This is the same class of bug as **#20675** (`hermes debug` credential check ignores pool) and **#15167** (`/usage` ignores pool for Codex) — but here it actively breaks runtime, not just diagnostics.

### Current resolution order in `resolve_anthropic_token()`

```python
def resolve_anthropic_token() -> Optional[str]:
    # 1. ANTHROPIC_TOKEN env var
    # 2. CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env var
    # 3. Claude Code credentials (~/.claude.json / ~/.claude/.credentials.json)
    # 4. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var
```

The `credential_pool` — which Hermes' own `hermes auth add anthropic --type oauth` writes to — is **not** in this chain. So a setup that uses *only* the Hermes-native PKCE flow (no Claude Code, no env vars, no API key) has zero of the four sources populated.

### Reproduction

On a fresh Hermes container (`v0.13.0 / 2026.5.7`), with no `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env vars and no `~/.claude/` files:

1. `hermes auth add anthropic --type oauth` → complete PKCE → succeeds. Token is written to `~/.hermes/auth.json` `credential_pool.anthropic[0]`.
2. Verify: `hermes auth status anthropic` → **`logged in`**.
3. Verify: `hermes auth list` → shows credential with `← active` marker.
4. Create a cron job:
   ```
   hermes cron create '*/5 * * * *' --skill <any-skill> 'do a thing'
   ```
5. Wait for tick or `hermes cron run <id>` to trigger immediately.
6. Job fails with:
   ```
   RuntimeError: No Anthropic credentials found. Set ANTHROPIC_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY,
   run 'claude setup-token', or authenticate with 'claude /login'.
   ```
   Stack: `cron/scheduler.py:1281 run_job → hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py:1194 resolve_runtime_provider → agent/anthropic_adapter.py raise AuthError`.

### Confusing partial behavior we observed

On one production deployment, two cron jobs scheduled 6 minutes apart on the same OAuth-only setup showed inconsistent behavior — earlier job failed with the above AuthError, later job succeeded. Likely cause: a second auth resolution path exists (`agent.auxiliary_client.resolve_provider_client` was visible in `WARNING agent.auxiliary_client: resolve_provider_client: anthropic requested but no Anthropic credentials found` log lines) that may or may not consult the pool, depending on the call site.

Net effect for operators: cron-driven workflows are flaky-unstable when authenticating via Hermes-native PKCE only, with no way to tell from the surface (`auth status` says `logged in`) that the runtime path won't actually find the token.

### Proposed fix

In `agent/anthropic_adapter.py:resolve_anthropic_token()`, add a step **between** current step 3 (Claude Code creds) and step 4 (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env) that:
1. Loads the credential_pool via `agent.credential_pool.load_pool()`.
2. Selects the active anthropic oauth entry (respecting `last_status != exhausted`).
3. If `expires_at_ms` is in the past, attempts refresh using the stored `refresh_token` against `https://login.microsoftonline.com`-equivalent for Anthropic (i.e. whatever the PKCE flow already uses for refresh).
4. Returns the (possibly refreshed) `access_token`.

This mirrors the `_prefer_refreshable_claude_code_token()` logic that already exists for the Claude-Code-file path — the same shape, but reading from `auth.json` instead.

Alternatively, the deeper refactor implied by #20675 / #15167: have a single canonical `resolve_credential(provider="anthropic")` that all entry points (auth.py status, anthropic_adapter token resolution, auxiliary_client, cron scheduler, /usage, debug) call. Today these paths drift apart.

### Affected version

- `hermes-agent v0.13.0 (2026.5.7)`

### Related issues

- #20675 — `hermes debug` doesn't see pool OAuth tokens (same bug pattern, diagnostic surface)
- #15167 — `/usage` ignores credential_pool for Codex (same bug pattern, different provider)
- #15080 — Anthropic OAuth via `~/.claude/.credentials.json` returns HTTP 400 (auth-related but different code path)

### Workaround in the wild

Operators currently work around this by either:
- (a) Setting `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in env (which defeats the purpose of using Hermes-PKCE subscription auth), or
- (b) Manually re-running `hermes auth add anthropic --type oauth` whenever the cron path stops working, which is fragile and requires browser PKCE interaction.

Neither is sustainable for headless cron-driven deployments. A pool-aware `resolve_anthropic_token()` would let `hermes auth add anthropic` actually do what it advertises end-to-end.

items.title: Feature Request: /plan and /build mode toggles with tool-level enforcement

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Summary

Add `/plan` and `/build` mode toggles to Hermes, giving the agent a constrained read-only planning mode (with tool-level enforcement) and a full-execution build mode — matching the developer workflow that OpenCode provides for agent-assisted coding.

---

## The Opportunity

Hermes already has a `/plan` skill (advisory — the agent is told to plan, not execute) and a robust `enabled_toolsets`/`disabled_toolsets` infrastructure for per-session tool restriction (currently used by cron jobs and kanban workers). What's missing is a **dynamic mode toggle** that switches between constrained (plan) and unconstrained (build) within a single session, with tool-level enforcement that the agent *cannot* ignore.

A plan/build mode pair would let users:
- Delegate complex features: "Plan the architecture for X" → review → "Now build it"
- Prevent premature execution during architectural exploration
- Use plan mode as a forced convergence gate before resource commitment
- Chain naturally with the existing `/ideation` skill and `/goal` command

---

## OpenCode Case Study

OpenCode implements `/plan` and `/build` as session-level mode toggles enforced at two layers:

### Layer 1: System Prompt
The mode instruction is baked into the system prompt, telling the model what behavioral constraints apply in each mode:
- **Plan mode**: You may read files, search the codebase, and produce plans. You may NOT write code or run commands.
- **Build mode**: Full execution capabilities. Implement the plan.

### Layer 2: Tool Schema Removal
Mutating tools are literally removed from the tool definition list passed to the model in plan mode. The LLM cannot call write/tool-execute functions because they are not in the schema. This is architectural enforcement, not behavioral suggestion.

### Benefits Observed
- **No accidental mutations** during exploratory planning — the agent literally can't write code or run commands it shouldn't
- **Cleaner separation of concerns** — users can safely request architectural exploration without monitoring what the agent does
- **Review-before-commit workflow** — plan is produced, reviewed, approved, then build executes it
- **Reduced cognitive load** — the mode switch is explicit and visible; the user knows what the agent can and can't do at any point
- **Parallel paradigm** — matches how humans approach complex work: understand first, then execute

---

## What It Would Take in Hermes

Hermes' architecture is different from OpenCode's — skills inject content as user messages, not system prompt modifications, and tool restrictions are static per-session. But the *infrastructure for enforcement already exists*.

### What Works Today (Configuration Only — No Changes)

- **`/plan` skill** already exists at `software-development/plan/` — injects read-only behavioral instructions (don't execute code, don't run mutating commands)
- **`/ideation` skill** for divergent creativity before planning
- **`structured-execution` skill** chains `/ideation` → `/plan` → `writing-plans` → `subagent-driven-development` → `/goal`
- The agent follows skill instructions in practice because it's an instruction-following LLM

**Limitation**: This is purely advisory. The agent *can* ignore plan instructions and start writing code. There's no runtime enforcement.

### What Requires Code Changes

#### 1. Add `/plan` and `/build` as Built-in CommandDef Entries

Currently `/plan` is only available as a skill command (loaded from `~/.hermes/skills/`). Adding it to the `COMMAND_REGISTRY` in `hermes_cli/commands.py` would make it a first-class slash command with gateway support, consistent across CLI and messaging platforms.

A `/build` command would exit plan mode and restore full execution capability.

#### 2. Wire Dynamic Tool Restriction into Skill/Session Lifecycle

The key infrastructure already exists:

- **`model_tools.py`**: `get_tool_definitions()` accepts `enabled_toolsets` to filter available tools
- **`run_agent.py` (line 4357)**: `set_thread_tool_whitelist()` / `clear_thread_tool_whitelist()` already provides runtime tool gating — currently used for background review agents. When called, tools outside the whitelist are denied at runtime with a descriptive error.
- **`AIAgent.__init__()`**: Accepts `enabled_toolsets` and `disabled_toolsets`

The gap is that these are set at session init time and never changed mid-session. A mode switch would need to:

a. **Store mode in session state** — a simple `mode: plan|build` field in the session config or SessionDB
b. **Re-resolve tool schemas on mode change** — call `get_tool_definitions(enabled_toolsets=...)` with the plan-mode toolset and pass the reduced schema to the next API call (or use the thread whitelist pattern for simpler enforcement)
c. **Optionally inject mode context** — append a system-level note about the current mode to the conversation

#### 3. (Optional) Add `enabled_toolsets` to Skill Frontmatter Metadata

A clean extension: allow skills to declare tool restrictions in their frontmatter:

```yaml
metadata:
  hermes:
    enabled_toolsets: ["file", "search", "web", "skills"]
```

When a skill is activated as a slash command, the skill dispatcher reads this field and applies the restriction for the duration of that skill's context. This would make `/plan` automatically restrict tools without any special handler code.

### Files to Change

| File | Change | Complexity |
|------|--------|------------|
| `hermes_cli/commands.py` | Add `CommandDef("plan", ...)` and `CommandDef("build", ...)` to `COMMAND_REGISTRY` | Trivial |
| `agent/skill_commands.py` | Read `metadata.hermes.enabled_toolsets` from skill frontmatter; call tool restriction hook | Small |
| `run_agent.py` or `model_tools.py` | Expose a method to update `enabled_toolsets` mid-session or wire the thread whitelist into the skill dispatch path | Small-Medium |
| `software-development/plan/SKILL.md` | Add `enabled_toolsets: ["file", "search", "web", "skills"]` to frontmatter (if the metadata path is adopted) | Trivial |

### What Doesn't Need to Change

- No new database tables or schemas
- No new plugin APIs
- No changes to cron, kanban, gateway, or any platform adapter
- No changes to the agent loop's core logic

---

## Discussion Invitation

This issue invites architectural discussion: Is the thread-whitelist approach the right enforcement mechanism? Should mode state be in SessionDB or config? Should plan-mode tool restrictions be defined by the skill or by a config-level `plan_toolsets` key?

I'm offering to develop the implementation myself — happy to fork and submit a PR once the approach is agreed upon.

---

## References

- Existing `/plan` skill: `software-development/plan/SKILL.md`
- `set_thread_tool_whitelist` in `run_agent.py` (around line 4357)
- `enabled_toolsets` in `AIAgent.__init__()` (around line 1134)
- Toolset definitions in `toolsets.py`
- COMMAND_REGISTRY in `hermes_cli/commands.py`

items.title: [Bug]: telegram.extra.base_url silently ignored — config propagation missing in gateway/config.py

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

PR #6851 added support for a custom Telegram Bot API `base_url` in the platform adapter ([`gateway/platforms/telegram.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/gateway/platforms/telegram.py#L1200), line 1200), but the configuration layer ([`gateway/config.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/gateway/config.py)) never propagates the value from `telegram.extra.base_url` into `platforms.telegram.extra`.

At runtime, `self.config.extra.get("base_url")` in `TelegramAdapter._start()` always returns `None` — the feature is silently non-functional. No error, no warning, just falls back to `api.telegram.org`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Add to `config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   telegram:
     extra:
       base_url: https://custom-proxy.example.com/bot
   ```
2. Start the Telegram gateway: `hermes gateway start`
3. Observe that all Bot API requests still go to `api.telegram.org`
4. Check `platforms.telegram.extra` in the resolved config — `base_url` is absent

### Expected Behavior

When `telegram.extra.base_url` is set in config.yaml, it should propagate to `platforms.telegram.extra` so that `TelegramAdapter._start()` picks it up and directs Bot API calls to the custom endpoint.

### Actual Behavior

The key `base_url` is silently dropped during config resolution. Only `guest_mode` and `disable_link_previews` are propagated.

### Affected Component

- [x] Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)
- [x] Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

- [x] Telegram

### Debug Report

Not applicable — bug identified through code inspection; no runtime crash to debug.

### Operating System

All (config propagation issue, not OS-specific)

### Python Version

`3.11.15`

### Hermes Version

`0.13.0`

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

Not applicable.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The bug is in [`gateway/config.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/gateway/config.py#L1045) at **line 1045**. The YAML config processing only propagates two specific keys:

```python
for _telegram_extra_key in ("guest_mode", "disable_link_previews"):
    if _telegram_extra_key in telegram_cfg:
        ...
        extra[_telegram_extra_key] = telegram_cfg[_telegram_extra_key]
```

Meanwhile, [`telegram.py` (line 1200)](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/gateway/platforms/telegram.py#L1200) correctly reads from `self.config.extra.get("base_url")` — but `extra` is never populated with `base_url` from the user config.

The helper [`_ensure_platform_extra_dict()` (line 77 of config.py)](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/gateway/config.py#L77) already exists for this purpose. The fix is to propagate all `telegram.extra` keys generically after the explicit per-key block.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add the following block after [line 1055 in `gateway/config.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/gateway/config.py#L1055):

```python
# Propagate telegram.extra keys (base_url, base_file_url, etc.)
# to platforms.telegram.extra so Telegram adapter can pick them up.
if _telegram_extra:
    plat_data, extra = _ensure_platform_extra_dict(
        platforms_data, Platform.TELEGRAM.value
    )
    for k, v in _telegram_extra.items():
        if k not in extra:
            extra[k] = v
```

This is forward-compatible — any future keys added to `telegram.extra` will automatically reach the platform adapter without code changes. See commit [`e376a9b2c957`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/e376a9b2c9575e34fa6ac132f499b354b7bd8ebb) for the `telegram.py` side that's already in `main`.

---

**Additional context:**

This fix was generated by Hermes Agent (model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash), tested end-to-end by the reporter, and confirmed working. The code was reviewed and manually verified by a human before submission.

The broader goal is to later migrate the agent into Docker and, by specifying the appropriate environment variables, obtain a fully working setup with Telegram base_url substitution — enabling Hermes to operate behind a custom Bot API endpoint in containerized environments.

items.title: hermes kanban diagnostics --severity filter is exact-match, not "at or above" as documented (kanban.py:1406)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

The `--severity` filter in `hermes kanban diagnostics` uses exact-match equality instead of the `>=` comparison its help text documents. This silently drops higher-severity diagnostics, which breaks monitoring scripts that rely on `--severity warning` as a catch-all for warning-and-above.

## Buggy code

`hermes_cli/kanban.py:1406`:

```python
kept = [d for d in diags_by_task[tid] if d.severity == sev]
```

This is an exact-match equality check.

## Documented behavior (contradicts the implementation)

`hermes_cli/kanban.py:360` (argparse help text for the `--severity` flag):

```
"Only show diagnostics at or above this severity"
```

The severity tuple `SEVERITY_ORDER = (\"warning\", \"error\", \"critical\")` is defined in `kanban_diagnostics.py` and is the natural ordering the filter should compare against.

## Live reproduction

On a real install with two `error`-severity diagnostics on the board:

```
$ hermes kanban --board <board> diagnostics --json | jq 'length'
2
$ hermes kanban --board <board> diagnostics --severity warning --json | jq 'length'
0
$ hermes kanban --board <board> diagnostics --severity error --json | jq 'length'
2
$ hermes kanban --board <board> diagnostics --severity critical --json | jq 'length'
0
```

Breakdown:

- No filter: 2 diagnostics returned.
- `--severity warning`: 0 returned. **Wrong** — should return 2, since both diagnostics are at or above warning.
- `--severity error`: 2 returned. Accidentally correct because both diagnostics happen to be error-severity (exact match).
- `--severity critical`: 0 returned. Correct only because no diagnostic is critical-level — but for the wrong reason (still exact-match).

The pattern: the filter only ever returns its exact-match level. Same problem at every severity.

## Real-world impact

This silently disables any watchdog cron or monitoring script that uses the default `--severity warning` flag to surface warning-and-above diagnostics. Operators get false-confidence silent runs while error- and critical-severity issues go undetected. The shipped semantics directly contradict the documented `\"at or above\"` semantics, so the failure mode is invisible without manually re-checking with no filter.

## Expected behavior

The filter should compare via `SEVERITY_ORDER` index — return diagnostics whose severity is at or above the requested level:

- `--severity warning` → `warning` + `error` + `critical`
- `--severity error` → `error` + `critical`
- `--severity critical` → `critical` only

Rough fix sketch:

```python
threshold = SEVERITY_ORDER.index(sev)
kept = [
    d for d in diags_by_task[tid]
    if SEVERITY_ORDER.index(d.severity) >= threshold
]
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.13.0 (2026.5.7)
- Python 3.11.15 (bundled venv) / 3.14.5 (system)
- OpenAI SDK 2.24.0
- OS: Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 (macOS)

## Why filed as an Issue

Filing as an Issue rather than a PR because Nous's contribution guidelines don't explicitly address PRs against undocumented CLI features, and `hermes kanban diagnostics` doesn't appear in the public CLI reference at https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/cli-commands. Happy to follow up with a PR if maintainers indicate that's preferred.

items.title: [Feature]: Config option to hide/disable built-in providers from the picker

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

The `/model` picker and `hermes model` list show ALL providers from the
hardcoded `CANONICAL_PROVIDERS` list + auto-discovered provider plugins, even
when the user has no credentials for them.

Example: a user with only `opencode-go` and one custom endpoint sees
`GitHub Copilot (16)` in the buttons — 16 models from the static
`_PROVIDER_MODELS["copilot"]` list.

Root cause in `list_authenticated_providers()` (model_switch.py ~line 1232):

    if store and hermes_id in store.get("credential_pool", {}):
        has_creds = True

The credential pool for "copilot" exists as an empty list `[]` in auth.json
(populated by suppressed_sources mechanism), so `"copilot" in {"copilot": []}`
evaluates to True. This makes copilot pass the credential filter despite
having no actual API keys or tokens.

No user-configurable mechanism to suppress entries.


### Proposed Solution

Proposed Solution:
Add a config option in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, e.g.:

yaml
providers:
  disabled:
    - copilot
    - copilot-acp
    - lmstudio

This would:
1. Filter out matching slugs from `list_authenticated_providers()` /
   `_build_provider_picker()`
2. Optionally skip loading/registering those provider plugins at discovery time
3. Still allow explicit `--provider copilot` usage via CLI — only hide from the
   picker

Or simpler: `hidden_providers` / `provider_blocklist` — even just filtering the

items.title: [Bug]: Codex usage_limit_reached 429 retries exhausted pool credential once before rotating

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

OpenAI Codex can return HTTP 429 with a structured error body like:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "usage_limit_reached",
    "message": "The usage limit has been reached"
  }
}
```

Hermes currently extracts only `error.code` / `error.error` into the credential-pool error context, so `error.type=usage_limit_reached` is lost. The central classifier sees HTTP 429 and treats it as a generic transient `rate_limit`.

That makes `_recover_with_credential_pool()` keep the same exhausted Codex credential on the first failure and only rotate after a second 429 in the same retry sequence. For Codex account usage windows this is not useful: the current OAuth profile is exhausted until reset, while other pool entries may still have available quota.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `openai-codex` with two or more OAuth entries in the credential pool.
2. Use an entry whose Codex quota is exhausted while another pool entry still has quota.
3. Trigger a Codex request that returns HTTP 429 with `error.type = "usage_limit_reached"`.
4. Observe the first recovery attempt retrying the same exhausted credential instead of marking it exhausted and rotating immediately.

A minimal unit repro is `_recover_with_credential_pool(status_code=429, has_retried_429=False, error_context={"reason": "usage_limit_reached"})`: today it returns `(False, True)` instead of rotating.

## Expected Behavior

A Codex `usage_limit_reached` 429 should be treated as account/window exhaustion for pool recovery. Hermes should mark that pool entry exhausted and rotate to the next available same-provider credential immediately.

## Actual Behavior

Hermes treats the response as a generic transient 429, retries the same credential once, and can appear stuck on an exhausted account even when `hermes auth list openai-codex` shows other accounts without limits.

## Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram and CLI can both hit the same core recovery path; the bug is in `run_agent.py`.

## Debug Report

N/A for this report. This was reduced to the recovery helper and covered with unit tests in the companion PR.

## Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04

## Python Version

Python 3.11+

## Hermes Version

`main` at d5416284f11ccbc735c8357f0ab35ce5f683ccc3

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

Known provider message:

```shell
HTTP 429: The usage limit has been reached
```

Known structured body field that is currently dropped:

```shell
error.type = usage_limit_reached
```

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Two details combine:

1. `AIAgent._extract_api_error_context()` ignores `payload["type"]`, so OpenAI's `usage_limit_reached` type does not reach the pool recovery code.
2. `_recover_with_credential_pool()` treats all 429s as transient `FailoverReason.rate_limit`, where the first 429 intentionally retries the same credential.

That first retry makes sense for throttling, but not for Codex `usage_limit_reached`, which is a quota-window exhaustion signal for the current account.

## Similar Issues / PRs Checked

This is intentionally narrower than the currently open related work:

- #26149 rotates immediately only when the current entry is already marked exhausted; it does not handle a fresh `usage_limit_reached` body on the first 429.
- #25733 aligns credential pools with runtime/fallback state; it does not change the `usage_limit_reached` classification/recovery behavior.
- #25277 loads pools during `/model` switch; different entry path.
- #24173 handles Codex Responses soft failures where HTTP status is 200 with `response.status=failed`; this issue is the HTTP exception path.
- #19608 fixes concurrent auth-store stale writes; different persistence race.
- #22778/#22792 fixed auxiliary-client cache pinning; this is the main agent recovery path.

Searches included `usage_limit_reached` with `first 429`, `second 429`, `retry same credential`, `rotate immediately`, and `The usage limit has been reached` + `credential pool` across open and closed issues/PRs.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

- Extract `payload["type"]` as the context reason when `code` is absent.
- In rate-limit pool recovery, if `error_context.reason` contains `usage_limit_reached` or the message contains `usage limit has been reached`, skip the first-same-credential retry and immediately call `mark_exhausted_and_rotate()`.
- Add regression tests for both context extraction and immediate rotation.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes; companion PR follows.

items.title: QQ Bot: File attachments cached but path not passed to agent, original filename lost

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

When users send file attachments (Excel, PDF, Word etc.) to Hermes via QQ Bot, the adapter downloads and caches them successfully but:

1. The cached local file path is never passed to the agent — the agent only sees `[Attachment: qqdownloadftnv5]` as text, with no way to read the file.
2. The cached filename loses its original extension (e.g. `成绩表.xlsx` becomes `doc_xxxx_qqdownloadftnv5`), because the filename is extracted from the CDN URL path (a non-semantic token) rather than the QQ API's `attachment.filename` metadata.

## Root Cause

Both issues are in `gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py`:

### Bug 1: Path not passed to agent

In `_process_attachments()`, the `else` branch (non-image, non-voice attachments) downloads the file via `_download_and_cache()` and only appends a text marker to `other_attachments`:

```python
else:
    cached_path = await self._download_and_cache(url, ct)
    if cached_path:
        other_attachments.append(f"[Attachment: {filename or ct}]")
    # cached_path is NEVER added to image_urls/media_urls
```

Meanwhile, images correctly populate `image_urls` and `image_media_types`, which get passed to `MessageEvent.media_urls`. The file paths are simply discarded.

### Bug 2: Original filename lost

In `_download_and_cache()`, the document branch extracts the filename from the CDN URL:

```python
else:
    filename = Path(urlparse(url).path).name or "qq_attachment"
    return cache_document_from_bytes(data, filename)
```

QQ's file CDN URLs (e.g. `grouptalk.c2c.qq.com`) have paths like `/.../qqdownloadftnv5` — no original extension. The actual filename from QQ API metadata (`attachment.filename`) is available in `_process_attachments` (as the `filename` variable) but never passed to `_download_and_cache()`.

## Impact

- User sends any non-image file (Excel, PDF, CSV, Word, etc.)
- Agent receives text like `[Attachment: qqdownloadftnv5]` with no file path → cannot read or process the file
- The cached copy has no extension → downstream tools (pandas, file type detection) fail
- No error or warning — the system behaves as if the file was never sent

## Related Issues

- **#14301** — "QQ Bot: File attachments downloaded but not passed to agent" — identifies Bug 1 (download success path)
- **#16979** — "QQ Bot: file attachments (PDF etc.) silently dropped when download fails" — mentions filename loss as root cause point 4 (but PRs #16990 and #17108 only fix the download-failure case, not the success path)

## Proposed Fix

Two changes in `gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py`:

### Fix 1: Pass cached path to agent

In `_process_attachments()`, append the cached path to `image_urls` (like images do):

```diff
 else:
-    cached_path = await self._download_and_cache(url, ct)
+    cached_path = await self._download_and_cache(url, ct, original_filename=filename)
     if cached_path:
         other_attachments.append(f"[Attachment: {filename or ct}]")
+        image_urls.append(cached_path)
+        image_media_types.append(ct)
```

### Fix 2: Preserve original filename

Add `original_filename` parameter to `_download_and_cache()`, use it with priority:

```diff
-    async def _download_and_cache(self, url: str, content_type: str) -> Optional[str]:
+    async def _download_and_cache(
+        self, url: str, content_type: str, original_filename: str = ""
+    ) -> Optional[str]:
```

```diff
     else:
-        filename = Path(urlparse(url).path).name or "qq_attachment"
-        return cache_document_from_bytes(data, filename)
+        name_to_use = original_filename or ""
+        if not name_to_use:
+            name_to_use = Path(urlparse(url).path).name or "qq_attachment"
+        return cache_document_from_bytes(data, name_to_use)
```

Both fixes are backward-compatible and do not affect image/voice handling.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.10.x (current upstream)
- QQ Bot platform (Official API v2)

items.title: [UX]: Kanban WebUI forced ALL-CAPS styling reduces readability and obscures exact task/profile text
items.body:
### Problem

The Kanban WebUI currently displays too much interface text in forced uppercase / ALL CAPS.

This makes the board harder to read during normal use, especially when there are many task cards, assignees, statuses, and metadata fields on screen. It also makes the interface feel visually noisy, as if every card is shouting.

This is not only a cosmetic preference. In a developer/workflow tool, exact text matters. Profile IDs, task titles, task IDs, commands, paths, and user-entered content should be displayed in the same case that users typed or that the backend stores.

Related history:
- #21506 mentions that the Kanban WebUI displays profile names in uppercase due to CSS styling, while users must type lowercase profile names exactly.
- #18498 describes a related dispatcher/profile case-sensitivity failure caused by inconsistent casing between Kanban/dashboard/profile validation paths.

### Expected behavior

The Kanban WebUI should use normal-case text by default.

Examples:
- `worker`, not `WORKER`
- `phantom`, not `PHANTOM`
- task titles shown as written
- task descriptions shown as written
- assignee/profile names shown exactly as canonical stored IDs
- input/dropdown values shown exactly as submitted/stored

Uppercase styling should only be used for very small decorative static labels where it does not affect readability or exact-value interpretation.

### Actual behavior

Many Kanban UI elements are visually forced into uppercase. This makes the board harder to scan and can obscure whether values are actually uppercase or only styled that way.

### Suggested fix

Audit the Kanban frontend for uppercase transforms, including:

- CSS: `text-transform: uppercase`
- Tailwind: `uppercase`
- JavaScript/TypeScript: `.toUpperCase()`

Remove forced uppercase from user-facing content fields, including:

- task titles
- task descriptions
- assignee/profile names
- task IDs
- status labels
- input fields
- dropdown values
- card metadata
- buttons/headers where readability is affected

If uppercase is kept anywhere, it should be limited to small static labels only.

### Why this matters

Kanban is a working interface that users may keep open all day. Readability matters. Forced ALL-CAPS reduces scanability, increases cognitive load, and makes exact case-sensitive values harder to understand.

### Environment

Hermes Kanban WebUI / dashboard.

items.title: [Bug]: Response truncated due to output length limit — still occurring after #7237 fix (re-opening closed issue)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

The error "Response truncated due to output length limit" persists despite previous fixes in #7242 and #9525, which were merged in response to the now-closed issue #7237.

The issue was closed by a maintainer last month with the explanation that it is "not a bug" but rather a context window limitation. However, extensive testing and user reports (see the 10+ comments since the closure) continue to reproduce the error across different models — including those with very large context windows (414k tokens, 131k tokens, and even Gemini 1.5 with 2M tokens). 

This suggests that while the **input context** might be sufficient, the **output token cap** or the **continuation logic** for long tool outputs/summaries is failing. This new issue is meant to re-surface the problem with specific reproduction data showing failures on fresh sessions with large-context models.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch `hermes chat` (CLI) or `hermes gateway start` (Telegram / Discord / Slack).
2. Trigger a tool call that returns a large, dense payload (e.g., >80KB).
   - *Example*: `mcp_mongodb_collection_schema` on a complex database collection.
   - *Example*: `read_file` on a large lockfile (e.g., `pnpm-lock.yaml` or `package-lock.json`).
3. Observe the agent stop mid-generation (often during a summary or a sub-agent's response) with:
   `:warning: Response truncated (finish_reason='length') - model hit max output tokens`
   `:warning: Truncated tool call response detected — refusing to execute incomplete tool arguments.`
   `Error: Response truncated due to output length limit`
4. This happens even on fresh sessions (low input context), ruling out simple history overflow.

### Expected Behavior

Long responses should be split into chunks or the continuation logic should reliably retry until a complete response is assembled. The 3-retry mechanism introduced in #7242 / #9525 should prevent hard truncation in all API modes (chat_completions and anthropic_messages) by detecting `finish_reason='length'` and requesting the remainder.

### Actual Behavior

The agent throws "Response truncated due to output length limit" and halts. The continuation/retry logic does not trigger effectively, or the truncated JSON/summary is rejected by the agent's core before it can be completed.

Confirmed still occurring in:
- qwen3.6-27b-fp8 (414k context) — @theogravity
- GLM-51-NVFP4 — @Damikk19
- gpt-oss-20b (131k context) — @kevinctofel
- aws-claude-opus-4-6 — @yangyang233333
- Gemini 1.5 Flash / Pro (2M context) — @poulpe-agent-repro
- custom provider: gpt-5.5 — @arsitekberotok

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, tool output handling, continuation logic)

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       <https://paste.rs/JFt5G>
agent.log    <https://paste.rs/Anyts>
gateway.log  <https://paste.rs/N8CNm>
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04

### Root Cause Analysis

The current logic fails to differentiate between "Context Window Full" (Input) and "Max Output Tokens Hit" (Output). 
- Many providers have a hard limit on single completion length (e.g., 4096 or 8192 tokens).
- When a tool returns a massive result (e.g., a 100KB schema), the model tries to process/summarize it and hits its output cap long before it exhausts its input context.
- The continuation loop's progressive max_tokens boost (capped at 32k per #9525) might be insufficient or is not correctly detecting truncation when it happens inside a tool-call or sub-agent structure.

### Proposed Fix

- **Intelligent Tool Output Management**: If a tool result exceeds a certain size (e.g., 50KB), save it to a temporary file and only inject a summary/snippet into the context to prevent the model from "choking" on the output generation.
- **Unify Continuation Logic**: Ensure `anthropic_messages` and `chat_completions` paths are perfectly synced regarding truncation detection and retry.
- **Configurable Output Caps**: Allow users to override the 32k boost cap or the default `max_tokens` for completions in `config.yaml`.
- **Improved Logging**: Surface the actual token counts (Output used / Max output) when a truncation occurs to distinguish from Input context limits.

items.body:
# /reload-skills does not update Tab completion for newly installed skills

## Description

After installing new skills and running `/reload-skills`, the command reports the new skills as added, but they do not appear in the Tab completion menu when typing `/` in the chat prompt. The only workaround is to restart the entire hermes session.

## Root Cause

In `cli.py`, the module-level variable `_skill_commands` is assigned at startup:

```python
# cli.py ~line 2149
_skill_commands = scan_skill_commands()
```

The Tab completion lambda captures this name:

```python
# commands.py SlashCommandCompleter
skill_commands_provider=lambda: _skill_commands
```

When `/reload-skills` is invoked, it calls `reload_skills()` in `agent/skill_commands.py`, which internally does:

```python
global _skill_commands
_skill_commands = {}
_skill_commands = scan_skill_commands()  # creates a NEW dict object
```

This updates the `skill_commands` module's own `_skill_commands`, but **cli.py's module-level `_skill_commands` still points to the old dict object** created at startup. The Tab completion lambda resolves `_skill_commands` from cli.py's scope, so it always reads the stale data.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start `hermes chat`
2. Install a new skill (e.g. copy a skill directory to `~/.hermes/skills/`)
3. Run `/reload-skills` — it prints "added N new skills"
4. Type `/` and press Tab — the new skill commands are missing
5. Restart hermes — now the new skills appear in Tab completion

## Suggested Fix

In `cli.py`'s `_reload_skills()` method, after calling `reload_skills()`, sync the module-level variable:

```python
def _reload_skills(self, ...):
    from agent.skill_commands import reload_skills, get_skill_commands

    result = reload_skills()

    # Sync cli.py's module-level _skill_commands so the
    # Tab-completion lambda picks up the updated dict
    global _skill_commands
    _skill_commands = get_skill_commands()

    ...
```

## Environment

- Hermes v0.13.0 (2026.5.7)

items.title: _host_key() returns dot-separated form ("hermes.fundraising") that violates Honcho workspace ID regex
items.body:
## Summary

`_host_key()` in `plugins/memory/honcho/cli.py:238` returns `f"{HOST}.{_profile_override}"` when a profile override is set (e.g. `hermes.fundraising` for the `fundraising` profile). That dotted string can end up as the `workspace_id` sent to Honcho's API via the fallback in `plugins/memory/honcho/client.py:373-378`:

```python
workspace = (
    host_block.get("workspace")
    or raw.get("workspace")
    or resolved_host         # ← falls back to _host_key() which has a dot
)
```

If a `honcho.json` host block doesn't have an explicit `workspace` field, the fallback returns the dot-form. Honcho's API rejects it with:

```
{'type': 'string_pattern_mismatch',
 'loc': ['body', 'id'],
 'msg': "String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$'",
 'input': 'hermes.fundraising'}
```

## Why this surfaces

Running with `--profile <name>` produces logs like:

```
WARNING plugins.memory.honcho: Honcho init failed:
[{'type': 'string_pattern_mismatch',
  'loc': ['body', 'id'],
  'msg': "String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$'",
  'input': 'hermes.<profile_name>'}]
```

Once per minute. The Honcho memory plugin silently disables itself but the warning floods the journal.

## Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with a non-default profile name, e.g. `myprofile`.
2. Initialize Honcho via the CLI (`hermes honcho setup`), but DO NOT manually set the inner `workspace` field in the host block.
3. Run with `--profile myprofile`.
4. Observe the warning in journal/logs.

## Workaround (what we do)

Manually set `honcho.json` → `hosts.<host_key>.workspace` to an underscore-only string (e.g. `hermes_myprofile`). The explicit field wins over the fallback chain.

## Proposed fix

One-line change in `plugins/memory/honcho/cli.py:238`:

```diff
-        return f"{HOST}.{_profile_override}"
+        return f"{HOST}_{_profile_override}"
```

Plus a one-time migration helper for existing installs whose `honcho.json` outer keys are the dot-form: rename `hosts."hermes.X"` → `hosts."hermes_X"`. The inner `workspace` field is already underscore-tolerant.

## Impact

Cosmetic for users who set the explicit `workspace` field (no functional break). Real breakage for users relying on the fallback (their Honcho integration silently disabled).

Happy to send a PR with the rename + migration helper if you'd like — let me know.

items.body:
## Bug Description

The `mcp_tool.py` hardcodes `_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL = 180` (3 minutes) for stdio/HTTP MCP servers.
When a Cron job runs at high frequency (e.g., `every 2m` or `every 1m`), it frequently collides with the mandatory reconnection window triggered by this keepalive cycle.

The reconnection process takes approximately **4 seconds**.
If the Cron job starts exactly during this window (which happens often due to the frequency resonance between 2m and 3m), the MCP tool call fails with a connection error or timeout.

## Reproduction
1. Configure a Docker MCP server (e.g., `docker-mcp`).
2. Create a Cron job with `every 2m` schedule calling an MCP tool.
3. Observe `agent.log`. The keepalive fires every 180s, causing a brief disconnect.
4. The Cron job hits this disconnect roughly 30-50% of the time, failing the tool call.

## Proposed Solution
Allow `_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL` to be configured via `mcp_servers` in `config.yaml`.

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  docker-mcp:
    command: docker
    args: ["mcp", "gateway", "run", "--profile", "default"]
    keepalive_interval: 600  # Default is 180. 0 to disable, or >300 to reduce collision frequency with 1m/2m/5m cron jobs.
```

## Impact
Users running high-frequency Cron jobs (e.g., trading bots, health checks) experience intermittent tool failures that are difficult to debug because the error only appears during the short reconnection window.

items.title: Gateway kanban dispatcher should handle corrupted default board DB without repeated tracebacks
items.body:
## Summary

When the gateway-embedded kanban dispatcher encounters a corrupted default board database, it logs a full traceback on every dispatch interval and keeps retrying indefinitely. The process remains alive, but the logs become noisy and there is no clear recovery guidance or automatic quarantine/recreation path.

## Observed behavior

With `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway: true` and the default dispatch interval, the gateway logs this once per minute:

```text
ERROR gateway.run: kanban dispatcher: tick failed on board default
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../gateway/run.py", line 4553, in _tick_once_for_board
    conn = _kb.connect(board=slug)
  File ".../hermes_cli/kanban_db.py", line 928, in connect
    apply_wal_with_fallback(conn, db_label=f"kanban.db ({path.name})")
  File ".../hermes_state.py", line 152, in apply_wal_with_fallback
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
sqlite3.DatabaseError: file is not a database
```

The affected file is the default board database:

```text
<hermes-home>/kanban.db
```

The file exists and has non-zero size, but it is not a valid SQLite DB. A valid SQLite file should start with `SQLite format 3\0`; the affected file did not. Opening it with Python sqlite raises:

```text
sqlite3.DatabaseError: file is not a database
```

## Expected behavior

The gateway should degrade gracefully when a board DB is corrupt or not a SQLite database. Ideally it should do one or more of the following:

- detect `sqlite3.DatabaseError: file is not a database` around `kanban_db.connect()` / WAL setup,
- log a concise actionable error instead of a traceback every minute,
- mark that board dispatcher as disabled until the file changes or the process restarts,
- provide a suggested recovery command or path,
- optionally quarantine the corrupt DB to something like `kanban.db.corrupt-<timestamp>` and recreate a fresh empty board when safe.

## Why this matters

The current behavior makes the gateway look unhealthy forever after a single corrupt default kanban DB. Users have to infer that the fix is to move or restore `<hermes-home>/kanban.db`, and the repeated stack traces obscure unrelated operational logs.

## Environment

- Hermes gateway with embedded kanban dispatch enabled
- Default board (`default`)
- `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway: true`
- `kanban.dispatch_interval_seconds: 60`

No local hostnames, usernames, domains, or machine-specific paths are included here.

items.body:
## Bug Description

When configuring `delegation.model` and `delegation.provider` in `config.yaml`, subagents spawned via `delegate_task` ignore the override and always use the parent agent's model and provider.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure delegation in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
```yaml
delegation:
  model: deepseek-v4-flash
  provider: deepseek
  base_url: https://api.deepseek.com/v1
  api_key: sk-<redacted>
```
2. Run a simple delegate_task test:
```
delegate_task(goal="Tell me your model name", toolsets=[])
```
3. Observe the result: `model: glm-5.1` (parent model) instead of `deepseek-v4-flash`.

## Expected Behavior

Subagent should use `deepseek-v4-flash` via `api.deepseek.com/v1` as configured in the delegation section.

## Actual Behavior

Subagent always inherits the parent's model (`glm-5.1`) and provider (`zai`).

## Investigation

I traced through the code and found:

### What works correctly
- `_load_config()` returns the correct delegation config with `base_url`, `api_key`, `model`, `provider`
- `_resolve_delegation_credentials()` correctly returns:
  ```python
  {"model": "deepseek-v4-flash", "provider": "custom", "base_url": "https://api.deepseek.com/v1", "api_key": "sk-...", "api_mode": "chat_completions"}
  ```
- These values are passed to `_build_child_agent()` as `override_provider`, `override_base_url`, `override_api_key`
- `_build_child_agent()` computes `effective_model = creds["model"]` (correct: `"deepseek-v4-flash"`)
- `AIAgent.__init__()` receives the correct `model`, `base_url`, `api_key`, `provider` parameters

### What goes wrong
The agent log shows the subagent ended up on `provider=copilot-acp model=glm-5.1`:
```
ERROR [subagent-0] API call failed after 3 retries. Could not start Copilot ACP command 'copilot'. | provider=copilot-acp model=glm-5.1
```

The parent agent runs on `zai/glm-5.1` (NOT copilot-acp), yet the child somehow gets `provider=copilot-acp`. The ACP transport inheritance in `_build_child_agent` (lines 1032-1053) should be cleared when `override_provider` is set (line 1045-1047), but the result suggests it is not being cleared properly.

Even after the most recent test (where the parent is on plain `zai` transport), the subagent still returns `"model": "glm-5.1"` — suggesting the delegation credentials may be resolved but then overwritten somewhere in `AIAgent.__init__()` or the fallback chain.

### Additional note
When `base_url` and `api_key` were empty strings (`''`) in config (the default), `_resolve_delegation_credentials` takes the `if configured_base_url:` branch as falsy, falls through to `if not configured_provider:` which also falls through, and returns all `None` values — meaning the child inherits everything from the parent. The `${ENV_VAR}` syntax was not expanded in the delegation section even though `_expand_env_vars` exists in the config loader. This may be a separate issue.

## Environment
- OS: macOS 26.3.1
- Hermes Agent: latest (installed via curl script)
- Parent model: zai/glm-5.1
- Configured delegation model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
- DeepSeek API verified reachable via curl (returns valid completions)

## Config (sanitized)
```yaml
model:
  default: zai/glm-5.1
  provider: zai
  base_url: https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/coding/paas/v4

delegation:
  model: deepseek-v4-flash
  provider: deepseek
  base_url: https://api.deepseek.com/v1
  api_key: sk-<redacted>
  inherit_mcp_toolsets: true
  max_iterations: 50
  child_timeout_seconds: 600
  max_concurrent_children: 3
  max_spawn_depth: 1
  orchestrator_enabled: true
```

items.body:
## Problem

When using `kanban create --workspace worktree`, the dispatcher resolves the worktree path as `Path.cwd() / ".worktrees" / task.id` (line 2667-2670 of `kanban_db.py`). Since the gateway process CWD varies between starts, worktrees end up in unpredictable locations:

```
~/.hermes/hermes-agent/.worktrees/           (gateway from hermes-agent dir)
~/projects/anamnesis/.worktrees/             (gateway from anamnesis dir)
~/.hermes/services/hermes-webui-cn/repo/.worktrees/  (gateway from webui dir)
```

Additionally, the auto-generated branch name is `wt/t_<task_id>` which is opaque in git history.

## Requested Features

### 1. `--workspace worktree:<path>` syntax

Mirror the existing `--workspace dir:<path>` pattern so users can pin worktree placement:

```bash
hermes kanban create "..." --workspace worktree:~/projects/anamnesis/.worktrees/t6-wire
```

The code already supports this — `resolve_workspace()` in `kanban_db.py` uses `task.workspace_path` when set. The CLI just needs to parse `worktree:<path>` the same way it parses `dir:<path>`.

### 2. `--branch <name>` flag for meaningful git history

```bash
hermes kanban create "..." --workspace worktree --branch wt/t6-wire
```

The worker would use this branch name when creating the worktree instead of auto-generating `wt/t_<task_id>`. This makes `git log --all` show meaningful branch names like `wt/t6-wire` instead of `wt/t_ac4b381c`.

## Impact

Without this, kanban multi-wave parallelism with worktrees requires manual workarounds: workers renaming branches via `git branch -m` in task bodies, verifying workspace paths match expectations, etc.

## Implementation Notes

- `hermes_cli/kanban.py` `WorkspaceAction` already parses `scratch|worktree|dir:<path>`. Extend to accept `worktree:<path>` and set both `workspace_kind=worktree` and `workspace_path`.
- For `--branch`, add an optional `branch_name` column to the kanban tasks table, or pass it through worker environment.

items.title: [RFC] Stage-Level Tool Whitelist: Reducing Decision Fatigue in AI Agents

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
# RFC: Stage-Level Tool Whitelist — Reducing Decision Fatigue

## Summary

Introduce **per-turn tool filtering** via a `tools` parameter in the pre-LLM hook (`pre_llm_call`), allowing hook callbacks to dynamically restrict the tool schema exposed to the model at each turn. This reduces decision fatigue (Statewright: 13B model 20%→100% correct rate) by compressing the decision space before the model reasons, not after.

---

## Motivation

Statewright (Qwen 2.5 13B) proved that constraining tool visibility per workflow stage dramatically improves agent reliability:

| | No constraints | Stage constraints |
|---|---|---|
| SWE-bench accuracy | 20% | **100%** |
| Avg tokens | 14,200 | 9,800 (-31%) |
| Invalid tool calls | 32% | 4% |
| Avg time | 48.2s | 37.6s |

**Root cause:** Decision space overload — each turn the model selects from the full tool list, wasting ~1/3 of tokens on wrong choices.

**Current Hermes gap:** `pre_llm_call` can inject context, but cannot reduce the tool schema. The model always sees all tools in `self.tools`, even in phases where most tools are irrelevant.

---

## Problem Statement

Hermes exposes the **full tool registry** to the model on every turn. For complex tasks (coding, research, multi-step workflows), this creates three failure modes:

1. **Decision space overload** — model wastes tokens selecting from irrelevant tools
2. **Attention dilution** — long tool schemas fragment model attention
3. **Loop hesitation** — no stage boundaries, model repeats non-productive actions

The existing `pre_llm_call` hook is architecturally capable but currently only supports context injection, not tool filtering.

---

## Proposed Solution

### Core Feature

Add support for a `tools` key in the `pre_llm_call` hook return value:

```python
# Existing (already supported):
{"context": "recalled text..."}  # inject into user message
"plain string"                    # alias for {"context": "..."}

# New:
{"tools": ["read_file", "search_files", "terminal"]}  # filter tool schema
```

When a `pre_llm_call` callback returns `{"tools": [...]}`, the returned list **replaces** the current turn's tool schema (filtered view, not all tools).

### Architecture

```
invoke_hook("pre_llm_call", ...)
  -> [callback returns {"tools": ["read_file", ...]}]
  -> filtered_tools = filter(self.tools, allowed=returned_tools)
  -> client.chat.completions.create(tools=filtered_tools, ...)
```

**Backwards compatible:** If no callback returns `tools`, behavior is unchanged (full tool list).

### Hook Execution Order

1. All registered `pre_llm_call` callbacks fire
2. Collect all returned `{"tools": [...]}` dicts (union semantics)
3. If allowed set is non-empty, apply filter before API call; otherwise use full list
4. Merge returned `{"context": ...}` strings into user message (existing behavior)

---

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Core (hermes_cli/plugins.py)

Modify `invoke_hook()` to:
1. Collect `tools` keys from `pre_llm_call` callback returns
2. Return `(results, allowed_tools)` where `allowed_tools: Set[str] | None`
3. Document new return key in hook docstring

### Phase 2: Agent Integration (run_agent.py)

1. Capture `allowed_tools` from `invoke_hook("pre_llm_call", ...)`
2. If non-empty, filter: `tools = [t for t in tools if t.function.name in allowed_tools]`
3. Pass filtered tools to `client.chat.completions.create(..., tools=filtered_tools)`
4. `self.tools` unchanged (remains authoritative for validation)

### Phase 3: Documentation

- Document `tools` key in hook docstrings
- Add example skill demonstrating stage-based tool filtering
- Update AGENTS.md with use case and limitations

---

## Limitations & Tradeoffs

| Limitation | Note |
|---|---|
| Advisory, not enforced | If model calls a filtered tool, `handle_function_call` still executes it. This prevents model confusion but doesn't hard-block. |
| Union semantics | Multiple callbacks returning different `tools` lists → union. May need intersection or last-wins if conflicts arise. |
| Breaking change | `invoke_hook()` return type changes from `List[Any]` to `Tuple[List[Any], Set[str] | None]` — callers must adapt. |
| Per-turn not per-message | If multiple messages sent in one turn, filtering applies to all equally. |

---

## Alternatives Considered

### 1. Per-turn `enabled_toolsets` parameter
Requires stateful `self.tools` mutation mid-session. More invasive to agent core.

### 2. Tool filtering in `transform_tool_result`
Wrong timing — model already saw full schema. Must filter before model reasons.

### 3. Provider-side tool filtering
Not universal across all providers. Hook approach is provider-agnostic.

---

## Open Questions

1. Union vs intersection semantics for multiple `tools` returns?
2. Should filtered-out tools appear in error messages if the model attempts to call them?
3. Should there be a priority/ordering mechanism (last-wins)?

---

## References

- Statewright experiment: https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/Klkq87U02EGWVFmBmqRYuA
- Existing hook system: `hermes_cli/plugins.py`
- Related: Context pollution defense, session health monitor

items.title: /codex-runtime codex_app_server silently skips migration when openai_runtime already set in config

items.body:
## Summary

`/codex-runtime codex_app_server` silently skips the migration step when the
user's config already has `model.openai_runtime: codex_app_server` set —
typically because the user set it manually in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
before running the slash command. The command reports "openai_runtime
already set to codex_app_server" with no migration output, and
`~/.codex/config.toml` never receives the managed block. The codex
runtime appears configured but is functionally inert.

## Repro

1. `hermes config set model.openai_runtime codex_app_server` (or edit `config.yaml` directly to set this)
2. Verify no `# managed by hermes-agent` block exists in `~/.codex/config.toml`
3. Start `hermes chat` and run `/codex-runtime codex_app_server`
4. Output: `✓ openai_runtime already set to codex_app_server` — no migration, no MCP callback registration, no plugin discovery
5. `grep "managed by hermes-agent" ~/.codex/config.toml` → empty

Expected: the slash command should run the migration regardless of whether the config value already matches, because the world state (managed block in `~/.codex/config.toml`, `[mcp_servers.hermes-tools]` callback, native plugin discovery, default permissions) is independent of the config value and may be missing or stale even when the value is correct.

## Root cause

In `hermes_cli/codex_runtime_switch.py:148`, `apply()` short-circuits when `new_value == current` and returns "already set" with no further action. The migration block at lines 200-247 — which writes the managed section to `~/.codex/config.toml`, registers the hermes-tools MCP callback, and discovers native plugins — is only reachable in the `current != new_value` transition branch.

The check conflates two semantically distinct conditions:
- (a) "the config value is what the user asked for"
- (b) "the world state — managed block, MCP server, plugins — is converged"

For `auto` → no-op these are equivalent (disabling doesn't touch `~/.codex/`). For `codex_app_server` → no-op they aren't: the user can absolutely have the config value correct but be missing the world-state side effects, especially when migrating an existing Hermes install where `~/.codex/config.toml` predates the runtime feature.

## Proposed fix

Fall through to the migration block when re-applying `codex_app_server` while skipping the config persist (no value-level change, no need to rewrite `config.yaml`). The migration is idempotent by design — `_strip_existing_managed_block()` removes any prior managed section before writing — so re-running is safe.

Surface message becomes "openai_runtime already set to codex_app_server — re-applying migration" so users see what happened.

The `auto` re-apply path remains the early-return short-circuit because disabling has no world-state side effects to converge.

## Why this matters

Pre-setting `model.openai_runtime: codex_app_server` in `config.yaml` (e.g. when scripting profile setup or cloning a profile that already had it set) is a reasonable thing to do — and is in fact how `hermes profile create <name> --clone` behaves when cloning from a profile that has codex runtime enabled. Combined with the silent no-op, users end up with a `codex_app_server` config value but no actual app-server runtime, falling through to `codex_responses` (Responses API direct) instead.

This is a footgun for the next user (Codex/HermesAgent operator) to hit.

A PR with the fix and a regression test (`test_reapply_codex_app_server_runs_migration`) is incoming, structured as a one-line semantic change with full coverage.

items.body:
## Summary

When the codex app-server runtime is active on a gateway / cron / non-CLI context (Discord, Telegram, Slack, scheduled jobs, etc.), codex's exec and apply_patch approval requests **silently fail closed** instead of either prompting the user or honoring `approvals.mode`. The bot appears responsive but cannot write files: from the user's POV, a write-requesting task produces no output, no error, and no surfaceable approval prompt anywhere.

## Repro

1. Configure Hermes with `model.openai_runtime: codex_app_server`
2. Run a gateway (Discord, Telegram, anything non-CLI):
   ```
   hermes gateway run -v
   ```
3. From the gateway-side, ask the bot to write a file:
   ```
   @bot please write a hello world script to /tmp/hi.py
   ```
4. Bot's response includes "patch rejected by user" (or for shell exec, a silent decline). No approval prompt is surfaced anywhere — not in the gateway channel, not in the gateway logs, not in the bot's response.

## Root cause

`run_agent.py:15779-15782` (current upstream main) constructs the `CodexAppServerSession` like this:

```python
try:
    from tools.terminal_tool import _get_approval_callback
    approval_callback = _get_approval_callback()
except Exception:
    approval_callback = None
self._codex_session = CodexAppServerSession(
    cwd=cwd,
    approval_callback=approval_callback,
)
```

`_get_approval_callback()` is wired by the interactive CLI thread via `set_approval_callback(self._approval_callback)` in `cli.py:7880`. The gateway path doesn't install a callback — there's no equivalent of `tools.terminal_tool.set_approval_callback()` call in any `gateway/` file. So `approval_callback` is `None` on the gateway path.

Inside `agent.transports.codex_app_server_session._decide_exec_approval()` (line 676) and `_decide_apply_patch_approval()` (line 698):

```python
if self._approval_callback is not None:
    try:
        choice = self._approval_callback(...)
        return _approval_choice_to_codex_decision(choice)
    ...
return "decline"  # fail-closed when no callback wired
```

So gateway-context codex tool requests always return `"decline"` — codex sees a synthetic "user denied" and proceeds in read-only mode, which gets surfaced as "patch rejected by user".

This is double-gating with a missing second gate: codex's own sandbox permission profile (`:read-only` / `:workspace` / `:danger-no-sandbox` in `~/.codex/config.toml`) is the user-configurable filesystem boundary; Hermes' approval router was meant to add a per-command interactive checkpoint *on top of* codex's sandbox. With no UI, the second gate doesn't ask — just denies.

## What I'd propose

When the user has explicitly opted out of Hermes approvals through any of the documented mechanisms — `approvals.mode: off` in config, `HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1` env var, or `/yolo` session toggle — collapse to codex's sandbox-only gating. Pass `request_routing=_ServerRequestRouting(auto_approve_exec=True, auto_approve_apply_patch=True)` to the session so codex's approval requests don't enter the Hermes approval flow at all.

Defaults (`approvals.mode: manual` or unset) preserve the current fail-closed behavior — this is a no-op for users who haven't explicitly opted out of approvals.

Semantics extension worth noting in release notes: "approvals.mode: off now also applies to codex app-server tool requests." Users who set `approvals.mode: off` for Hermes-native tools may not have considered the codex-runtime case, but the consistent semantics is probably what they'd want.

## Why not just wire the gateway approval callback?

Routing codex's exec/apply_patch approvals through Discord-side messages (e.g. with `/approve` and `/deny` slash commands) is a real feature but a much bigger one — codex's approvals are per-tool-call and would need async correlation between the codex turn loop and the gateway's message lifecycle. It belongs in its own PR (and probably its own issue first). The "honor approvals.mode/yolo" fix unblocks the immediate "my bot is silently read-only" case and is something users can take action on today.

A PR with the fix and 5 new integration tests covering each opt-out mechanism (config "off", YAML 1.1 `False`, env var, session yolo) plus regression coverage of the default fail-closed path is incoming.
